vappitaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Past participle agreeing with bījaṃ (nominative singular neuter). Final 'a' plus 'ta' causes gemination of 'p'.
vappitaṃ.example_1: Sukhette vappitaṃ bījaṃ, sayambhumhi aho mama [ahosi me (syā.)].
vappitaṃ.translation_1: Like a seed sown in a good field, it is mine in the Self-Become One.

kampalā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Here kampalā is nominative plural (with the -a > -ā ending), listed with other textiles in the Apadāna verse. The spelling with p for b is a variant. In PEU, kambala can also be a proper name (a dragon), but here it is the common noun.
kampalā.translation_2: rugs, fine silk, and cloth from China, fibrous cloth and yellow garments.

paṇḍupāvurā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound of paṇḍu (pale yellow) and pāvura (cloak, garment). Nominative plural in the text.
paṇḍupāvurā.translation_2: rugs, fine silk, and cloth from China, fibrous cloth and yellow garments.

saṃpūretvā.meaning_2: having filled; having made full; having fulfilled
saṃpūretvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive in -tvā of the causative saṃpūreti. In the text it occurs in a verse about offering food; a comment on the exact sense (filling the bowl, fulfilling a vow) is uncertain from the single line.
saṃpūretvā.translation_1: foods that were soft, and hard foods too, well-prepared food and drink to taste.

vicittamalyavitatā.meaning_2: spread with varied garlands; strewn with colourful flowers
vicittamalyavitatā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Vocative plural in the verse; malya is the Sanskritised form of māla (garland).
vicittamalyavitatā.translation_2: and with diverse garlands spread out; let all be carried over head.

dadāmiha.meaning_2: I give here; here I give
dadāmiha.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of dadāmi (present 1st singular of dadāti) + iha. The text has the variant dadāmihaṃ, glossed dadāmi taṃ. Meaning: offering the best gift here for the sake of supreme awakening.
dadāmiha.translation_1: Making the rocky mountains shout and likewise making dense hills roar,

yettha.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of the relative pronoun ya with the indeclinable ettha; used in verse for the usual yattha.
yettha.example_2: Yettha pacchimakā sattā, sotāpannā bhavantu te.
yettha.translation_2: I gave the gifts that should be given, fully fulfilling the precepts.

vidiya.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Probably a variant reading (sī. phanditāni; ka. jitabandhitāni) of jitaphanditāni in the verse; treated here as a past participle of vindati meaning 'found; obtained; known'. Uncertain.
vidiya.example_1: Hitvā papañce jitaphanditāni [vidiya phanditāni (sī.) jitabandhitāni (ka.)], tatheva bodhiṃ anupāpuṇiṃsu.
vidiya.translation_1: Abandoning obstacles, throbbing conquered, thereby indeed they achieved Awakening.

suññatappaṇīhitañcānimittaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of suññata + paṇīhitaṃ, ca and animittaṃ; variant reading at Ap 133 is suññappaṇidhiñca tathānimittaṃ. Accusative singular; the 'ca' joins the three meditative objects (suññata, paṇihita, animitta).
suññatappaṇīhitañcānimittaṃ.translation_1: 133. “In a Victor’s dispensation practicing merit, aspiration and thus gaining signs,

āsevayitvā.meaning_2: having practised; having cultivated; having devoted oneself (to); having associated (with)
āsevayitvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative absolutive in -tvā. Locative absolute phrase āsevayitvā jinasāsanamhi = 'having practised in the Victor's dispensation'. Written together in the text, sometimes separated as āsevayitvā.
āsevayitvā.translation_2: 133. “In a Victor’s dispensation practicing merit, aspiration and thus gaining signs,

vijjalantā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Probably a compound of vijjā + lanta (shining), i.e. 'radiant with wisdom', used of Paccekabuddhas. Feminine plural in -ā with a masculine or neuter nominative plural; the PEU gloss supports 'brilliant'; uncertain.
vijjalantā.example_2: Dīpā parattha idha vijjalantā, paccekabuddhā satataṃ hitāme.
vijjalantā.translation_2: Lamps shining the light of ultimate truth here, these Lonely Buddhas are constantly honored.

lokasudakkhiṇeyyā.meaning_2: worthy of the world's best offerings; most worthy of gifts from the world
lokasudakkhiṇeyyā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Bahubbīhi compound describing paccekabuddhas; nominative plural in the text. Sudakkhiṇeyya = su + dakkhiṇeyya (worthy of gifts).
lokasudakkhiṇeyyā.translation_2: Free of Doubt and Good for the World to Look At, these Lonely Buddhas are constantly honored.

vajalā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Only in a list of fish; the variant reading is jalajā, which makes the meaning clear. Unidentified species, perhaps 'valaja'.
vajalā.example_1: 145. ‘‘ Pāṭhīnā pāvusā macchā, balajā [vajalā (sī. syā.) jalajā (pī.)] muñjarohitā;
vajalā.translation_1: Sheatfish, pāvusa, valaja, reed-fish, red-fish and maggura

vaggulā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The text reads vaggulā, which is nominative plural of vaggula (a masc a-stem) or of vaggulī (a fem ī-stem). The variant vagguḷā is also given. Here the bats are said to beautify the ashram; the meaning 'bat' fits the context.
vaggulā.example_1: Vaggaḷā [vaggulā (sī.) vagguḷā (syā.) maggurā (theragāthā)] papatāyantā, sobhayanti [papatāyanti, sobhayantā (ka.)] mamassamaṃ.
vaggulā.translation_1: are flowing with the current there, making my ashram beautiful.

aṅkolā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Tree name; the form in the text is nominative singular feminine. A masculine aṅkola is also found.

uddhālakā.meaning_2: name of a tree (perhaps the golden shower tree, Cassia fistula); golden shower
uddhālakā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Listed among tree names in a forest description. Nominative plural ending -ā in the text.
uddhālakā.example_2: 153. ‘‘ Uddhālakā ca kuṭajā, kadambā vakulā bahū;
uddhālakā.translation_2: Golden shower, winter cherry, kadam and Spanish cherry trees

kadalimātuluṅgiyo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Two kinds of plant, banana and citron, joined in one compound. Nominative plural in the verse; the ending -iyo can also be read as accusative plural.
kadalimātuluṅgiyo.translation_2: Ālaka and isimugga, banana, also citron trees

mulāḷiyo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Nom. plural mulāḷiyo (with retroflex ḷ for l) in the verse. Refers to lotus stalks/roots growing and being cleansed in the water.
mulāḷiyo.translation_2: Pink lotuses germinate there; the lotus roots are being cleansed.

siṃghāṭipattamākiṇṇā.meaning_2: strewn with siṃghāṭī leaves; covered with siṃghāṭī petals
siṃghāṭipattamākiṇṇā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Bahubbīhi compound describing taḷāka; feminine nominative plural agreeing with the subject. ākiṇṇa = strewn, covered (pp of ākirati).
siṃghāṭipattamākiṇṇā.translation_1: Singhāṭi leaves are strewn about, making that tank so beautiful.

uttalī.meaning_2: name of a flowering plant; river-branch flower
uttalī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A plant name in a list of flowers in the Apadāna verse; the reading uttuli also occurs. Nom. sg. in the text.

saṃgulā.meaning_2: fork-tailed catfish; a kind of fish
saṃgulā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Nominative plural in the verse. PEU suggests derivation from saka + ula, but this is uncertain; no verbal root fits.
saṃgulā.example_1: Saṃgulā maggurā [maṅgurā (sī. ka.)] ceva, vasanti taḷāke tadā.
saṃgulā.translation_1: are living in that tank there then.

poṭṭhasīsā.meaning_2: name of a bird; kind of bird
poṭṭhasīsā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is nominative plural (poṭṭhasīsā) in a list of birds. The related entry poṭṭhasīsaka means a peasant bird.
poṭṭhasīsā.example_2: 163. ‘‘ Kosikā poṭṭhasīsā ca, kurarā senakā bahū;
poṭṭhasīsā.translation_2: Owls and poṭṭhasīsas too, numerous hawks, also osprey,

rohiccā.meaning_2: a kind of antelope; swamp deer
rohiccā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it appears as rohiccā, which is nominative plural. The word is probably a derivative of rohita (red deer) with the suffix -ya.
rohiccā.example_2: Rohiccā sukapotā [suttapotā (syā.)] ca, upajīvanti taṃ saraṃ.
rohiccā.translation_2: rohicca-deer, suggapotas are living on that lake there then.

āluvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A plant name in a list of corms. The form could also be read as a plural nominative in -ā; the PEU treats āluva as a masculine or neuter noun from √al.
āluvā.example_2: 170. ‘‘ Āluvā ca kaḷambā ca, biḷālītakkaḷāni ca;
āluvā.translation_2: Bindweed, also titan arum, bilāni, takkaḷāni bulbs jīvaka and sahaka plants

kaḷambā.meaning_2: titan arum; kaḷamba plant (a kind of plant); shoot sprouting from a palm nut
kaḷambā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In these Apadāna verses it is listed among plants. PEU gives kaḷamba as masc/nt; the form here is nominative singular in -ā, probably a sandhi or m.c. variant. Some editions read kaḍamba. Could alternatively be read as kaḷambā fem.
kaḷambā.example_2: 170. ‘‘ Āluvā ca kaḷambā ca, biḷālītakkaḷāni ca;
kaḷambā.translation_2: Bindweed, also titan arum, bilāni, takkaḷāni bulbs jīvaka and sahaka plants

ajjhogahiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 1st singular of ajjhogāhati (adhi + ava + √gāh). The form is ajjhogāhiṃ with the -ṃ of the ending; the sandhi of adhi + ava + gāh gives ajjhogāh-. In the verses it describes entering the forest.
ajjhogahiṃ.translation_2: Taking ascetics’ requisites I proceeded into the woods.

maddasī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] 2nd singular present maddasi, standing for the 3rd singular in the verse; the PEU splits it as madda + a + si. Another reading is maddasī = maddasi + ī.
maddasī.translation_2: with that knowledge, Omniscient One, you crush rivals and heretics.”

accugato.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of accu + gata, the old negative prefix accu- ('beyond, out of'). Nominative singular used of a mountain rising out of the water. Sometimes analysed as ati + gata or as accuggata; the sense is 'come up out of'.
accugato.translation_1: in the great ocean for as long as eighty-four thousand aeons.

olokayī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] 3rd singular aorist of the causative olokayati (ava + √lok + *e). The reading olokayī is a variant of olokayi; PEU analyses it as ava + loka + ṇaya, i.e. the same causative formation. Used of the Buddha surveying the world.
olokayī.translation_2: arising from his meditation, surveyed the whole world, that Victor.

nisiditvā.meaning_2: having sat down; having seated oneself
nisiditvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive in -itvā from the root √sad with the prefix ni; the present stem nisīdati uses the strengthened form nisīda-. The related dictionary entry gives the base as √sad + a > sīda (irreg).
nisiditvā.translation_1: sitting in the monks’ Assembly right then made manifest a smile.

aḷārapamhā.meaning_2: with thick eyelashes; having luxuriant eyelashes
aḷārapamhā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Bahubbīhi describing beautiful women in an Apadāna verse. The text shows the masculine plural form aḷārapamhā agreeing with hasulā. aḷāra is 'dense, thick'; pamha is 'eyelash'.
aḷārapamhā.translation_2: with long eyelashes, lovely smiles and slim waists, pleasant to look at,

phālaye.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Optative 3rd singular phālaye in the text, used in a simile of splitting a banana tree; causative of phalati.
phālaye.example_2: 272. ‘‘ Yathā sāratthiko poso, kadaliṃ chetvāna phālaye;
phālaye.translation_2: 272. Just as a man, wanting its pith, who chops and splits a banana tree,

paphussanti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading for phusanti; √phus with doubled initial consonant after the prefix pa. Third person plural in the text.
paphussanti.example_1: Sabbā velaṃva phusanti [sabbāva velaṃ phusanti (sī.), sabbā velaṃ paphussanti (syā.)], sañcuṇṇā vikiranti tā.
paphussanti.translation_1: when they do come onto the shore, they are crushed to bits and scattered.

sañcuṇṇā.meaning_2: crushed to powder; pulverised; smashed to bits; scattered
sañcuṇṇā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Past participle used as an adjective; nominative plural agreeing with tā. Formed with saṃ- + cuṇṇa (powder).
sañcuṇṇā.example_2: Sabbā velaṃva phusanti [sabbāva velaṃ phusanti (sī.), sabbā velaṃ paphussanti (syā.)], sañcuṇṇā vikiranti tā.
sañcuṇṇā.translation_2: when they do come onto the shore, they are crushed to bits and scattered.

sañcuṇṇāva.meaning_2: as if crushed to powder; as if ground to dust
sañcuṇṇāva.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of sañcuṇṇā (nominative plural of the past participle sañcuṇṇa, 'crushed to powder') + iva, 'like, as if'. Predicative in the clause sañcuṇṇāva bhavanti te, 'they become as if crushed to powder'.
sañcuṇṇāva.translation_2: having come into your presence, they get thoroughly crushed by you.

osadho.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Nominative singular in the text. In the simile osadho sabbapāṇinaṃ means "medicine for all living beings". Sometimes spelled osadha, neuter; also found as osadhī.

nuloketvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant of anuviloketvā (prefixed with nu- for anu-), as the text itself notes with viloketvā (sī. syā.), nuloketvā (ka.). Absolutive in -etvā of a causative-type form; root and construction are uncertain.
nuloketvā.translation_1: surveying the four directions then growls three times his mighty roar.

kittayuṃ.meaning_2: praised; celebrated; spoke of with praise
kittayuṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 3rd plural, causative stem kittaya- from √kitt. Occurs with lokanāyakaṃ as object: 'praised the world leader'. The PEU entry splits it as kitta + ṇaya + uṃ.

sampamaddāmi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] 1st person singular present in the text (sampamaddāmi); the lemma is the 3rd singular. The PEU glosses it as 'effectively oppress and destroy'.
sampamaddāmi.translation_2: 350. Today I’m the Dhamma’s general in the Buddha’s dispensation.

ussīsamhi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Locative singular in the text, in the phrase ussīsamhi karomi. Possibly a compound with ud + sīsa, but treated here as a simple noun.
ussīsamhi.translation_2: Having called to mind my karma, Gotama, Bull of the Śākyas,

tūresu.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Locative plural in the text (vajjamānesu tūresu). The PEU gives tūra as the instrument itself and tūriya as its sound.
tūresu.example_2: 378. ‘‘ Vajjamānesu tūresu, devā tūrāni [turiyesu, devā turiyāni (sī. syā.)] vajjayuṃ;
tūresu.translation_2: 378. When the drums were being beaten, the devas then also beat on drums.

sampabujjhatha.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] 2nd person plural present in the text (buddhopi sampabujjhatha), though it could also be read as 3rd singular with a variant ending; from the same family as pabujjhati.
sampabujjhatha.translation_2: Upon hearing the sound of both, the Buddha himself then listened.

paghaṭṭenti.meaning_2: pushes; jostles; rubs against; collides with
paghaṭṭenti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Third person plural present of the causative paghaṭṭeti (cf. paghaṭṭenti in the Apadāna verse). Alternative analysis as √ghaṭṭ 2 possible. The verb means 'to push, jostle, strike against'.
paghaṭṭenti.example_2: Aññamaññaṃ paghaṭṭenti, ākiṇṇaṃ hoti laṅkataṃ [taṃ tadā (sī.), satatā (syā.), saṅkaraṃ (?)].
paghaṭṭenti.translation_2: where they gather, one another; the city was very crowded.

hatthissarathasaṃkulaṃ.meaning_2: crowded with elephants, horses and chariots; full of elephants, horses and chariots
hatthissarathasaṃkulaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Describes the city (nagaraṃ) in the text; the word agrees with nagaraṃ in the neuter nominative/accusative singular. The first member is hatthī (elephant), with the final -ī shortened in the compound.
hatthissarathasaṃkulaṃ.translation_1: “Of such a sort was my city, crowded with elephants, horses, and chariots.

brāhmaññakulasambhūto.meaning_2: born into a brahmin family; arisen from a brahmin family
brāhmaññakulasambhūto.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of brāhmaññaṃ + kula + sambhūta. Describes the Bodhisatta's brahmin birth; nominative singular in the verse.
brāhmaññakulasambhūto.translation_2: “Born into a brahmin family, I had a massive heap of gems.

pupphehacchādayī.meaning_2: covered with flowers; overspread with flowers
pupphehacchādayī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of pupphehi (instrumental plural of puppha) + acchādayī (aorist 3rd singular of acchādeti, 'covered'). The variant reading pupphehi chādayī is also found.
pupphehacchādayī.translation_2: covered the entire Buddha-retinue with flowers at that time.

kittayī.meaning_2: speaks of; praises; declares; makes known
kittayī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist form in the text: kittayī = 'spoke of; praised'. PEU suggests a causative of kitteti.

kittayi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 3rd singular of the causative verb kitteti (from √kitt). The form occurs in the Apadāna verses.

kitvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading; the text also gives kītvā and kitvā. Absolutive of kiṇāti (√kī, buy), used with satasahassena (for a hundred thousand).
kitvā.translation_1: I spent a hundred thousand coins and built that monastic ashram.

vikkhālayiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the verse it is used as a 1st singular aorist ('I washed away the stains'), so vikkhālayiṃ is a phonetic variant of vikkhālesiṃ (vikkhāleti).
vikkhālayiṃ.translation_2: “Searching for the unconditioned, I washed away all of my stains.”

tāvadūraphale.meaning_2: whose fruit lasts that long; with fruit lasting so long
tāvadūraphale.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Locative singular absolute construction (tāvadūraphale sati) meaning "while/as long as the fruit lasts". Compound of tāva + dūra + phala.
tāvadūraphale.translation_2: “The gods are looking after that as long as the fruit may last there.”

vijaṭayiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text the form is vijaṭayiṃ, aorist 1st singular, with variant reading vijanayiṃ; the meaning is uncertain, perhaps 'I analysed' or 'I unravelled' the four fruits and the teachings. The PEU entry suggests a causative of jaṭa 'tangle'.
vijaṭayiṃ.example_1: Caturo ca phale sabbe, dhammevaṃ vijanayiṃ [vijaṭayiṃ (ka.) balākānaṃ vijāyanūpamāya saṃsandetvā attho veditabbo] ahaṃ.
vijaṭayiṃ.translation_1: “emptiness, the absence of marks, suchness, intentionality.”

siṅghāṭaṃ.meaning_2: four-way junction; crossroads; court of law
siṅghāṭaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text. In the Apadāna verse iddhipādañca siṅghāṭaṃ, the image is of a crossroads (or court) made of the iddhipādas and the dhammavīthi. The PEU gives masc/nt; here taken as nt.
siṅghāṭaṃ.translation_2: “Your court of law consists of the nine-fold teaching of the Buddha,”

vihārañcappaṇīhitaṃ.meaning_2: the dwelling which is free from desire; desireless abiding
vihārañcappaṇīhitaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Vihārañca + appaṇīhitaṃ; appaṇīhita = 'not directed, free from longing'. Accusative singular; part of the triad suññatā, animitta, appaṇīhita.
vihārañcappaṇīhitaṃ.translation_2: “desirelessness and cessation: all of these form your Dhamma-hut.”

porohicco.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Derived from purohita with the suffix -ya (ṇya). Nominative singular in the text, describing a brahmin adviser.
porohicco.example_2: Kolito nāma nāmena, porohicco tavaṃ mune.
porohicco.translation_2: “Bearer of the ancient lineage, hard to approach, of mighty power,”

āsahaṃ.meaning_2: I was able (to); I endured (in the course of) a thousand
āsahaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Probably a sandhi of āsahaṃ (1sg aorist of √sah) with sahassaṃ (a thousand), as the PEU entry āsahassa suggests. Alternatively an aorist first singular 'I endured; I was able' standing alone. The text is corrupt in these Apadāna verses.

sayambhumasādayiṃ.meaning_2: I approached the self-awakened one; I went near the Buddha
sayambhumasādayiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of sayambhuṃ (accusative singular of sayambhu, 'self-awakened one') and asādayiṃ (aorist 1st singular of sādayati, 'approached; drew near'). Accusative object with a 1st person verb.
sayambhumasādayiṃ.translation_2: ““We’ll bring our cities all to ruin; let’s seek the pardon of that sage.””

āsādito.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Past participle used passively with mayā: 'the Buddha was attacked by me'. Nominative singular masculine modifying buddho.
āsādito.example_2: 561. ‘‘ Āsādito mayā buddho, ghoro uggatapo jino;
āsādito.translation_2: ““If we don’t make him understand, that Self-Tamed One, Self-Controlled One,””

sumekhalo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name of a king in the Apadāna list. Nominative singular in the text. The PEU glosses it as 'one with a beautiful girdle' (su + mekhala), but here it functions as a name.
sumekhalo.example_2: 563. ‘‘ Sumekhalo kosiyo ca, siggavo cāpi sattako [sattuko (sī.)];
sumekhalo.translation_2: Sumekhala, Kosiya, Siggava, and also Sattaka;

āsādayitvā.meaning_2: having harassed; having insulted; having annoyed
āsādayitvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive in -itvā of the causative āsādayati (ā + √sad, *e). Formed on the present stem sādaya-.
āsādayitvā.translation_2: having harassed the seers, they came to grief with their kingdoms.

sannipātayiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 1st singular causative of sannipātayati (saṃ + ni + pat + *e). The text reads purise sannipātayiṃ, 'I assembled the people'. The PEU splits it as saṃ + ni + pata + ṇaya + iṃ. Could also be analysed as an aorist of sannipatati, but the causative sense suits the context best.

mabraviṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of idaṃ + vacanaṃ + abraviṃ; the text's mabraviṃ is a variant of abraviṃ, 1st person singular aorist of brūti. The sentence translates as 3rd plural because vacanamabravuṃ is given.
mabraviṃ.translation_1: falling down at the Buddha’s feet, they spoke these words:

abbhuggami.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 3rd singular of abbhuggacchati (= abhi + u + gacchati), with the k of the root becoming g. Used with nabhaṃ, 'rose up into the sky'.

vācāsabhimudīrihaṃ.meaning_2: the speech of the noble ones, the best of words, that was uttered; the excellent speech of the sages, uttered
vācāsabhimudīrihaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Probably vācā + asabhiṃ + udīrihaṃ; asabhiṃ = asabhaṃ, 'bull-like, noble, best' (cf. vṛṣabha). The verse describes the Buddha's speech. Could also be analyzed as vācāya asabhiṃ udīrihaṃ. Sandhi form; the exact division is uncertain.
vācāsabhimudīrihaṃ.translation_2: Having heard the words of the devas, that majestic speech they uttered,

upānayi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 3rd singular in the text (upānayi). PEU analyses it as root √nī with prefix upa-ā.

kappasagasse.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The text reads kappasagasse, a variant spelling; the Syā. and Ka. editions and the commentary gloss tiṃsamatte kappasagasse, i.e. kappa + sahassa. Locative plural in the sentence, in the phrase tiṃsakappasahassāni (thirty thousand aeons).
kappasagasse.translation_1: For thirty thousand aeons he will exercise divine rule.

ārūhi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] 2nd singular aorist in -i (like akāsi), here used of one person climbing aboard a boat; 3rd singular would be ārūhi too. From ā + √ruh, cf. ārūḷha.
ārūhi.example_2: 631. ‘‘ Āgantvāna ca sambuddho, ārūhi tañca nāvakaṃ;
ārūhi.translation_2: When the Sambuddha had arrived, he climbed onto that boat.

nāvakaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text (ārūhi taṃ nāvakaṃ). The PEU entry gives feminine 'noble boat', but the -ka suffix and the accusative -aṃ can be masculine or neuter; here taken as masculine. Perhaps = nāvā.
nāvakaṃ.example_2: 631. ‘‘ Āgantvāna ca sambuddho, ārūhi tañca nāvakaṃ;
nāvakaṃ.translation_2: When the Sambuddha had arrived, he climbed onto that boat.

nāvasaṇṭhitaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Describes a divine mansion (byamhaṃ). Accusative singular agreeing with sukataṃ. nāvā is the oblique form of the feminine noun nāvā before the compound member.
nāvasaṇṭhitaṃ.translation_2: A divine mansion will arise for you, well-made, boat-shaped;

parivimbhitā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading at this point; the text has parivimbhitā which is nominative plural, agreeing with the plural subject te. Possibly also read as an adjective meaning 'mocked'. The root √vimbh is not in the DPD root list, so the root fields are uncertain.
parivimbhitā.example_1: Sabbe te buddhanāgassa, na hontu paṇidhimhi te ’[na honti parivimbhitā (syā.), na honti paṇidhimhi te (ka.)].
parivimbhitā.translation_1: yet all of them are not equal to the might of the Buddha-elephant.

ekatthambhikattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of the elder Ekatthambhika; Ekatthambhika Thera's apadāna
ekatthambhikattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of the Apadāna section for the elder Ekatthambhika; nominative singular. Ekatthambhika may itself be a name meaning 'one-post' or 'single-support'.

upacelā.meaning_2: name of a universal monarch; name of a future Buddha's disciple
upacelā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name. The text has the nominative plural upacelā, referring to four individuals named Upacela in a past aeon. The name may be a compound (upa + cela), but the parts are uncertain.
upacelā.translation_2: in the sixty-thousandth aeon, there were four named Upacela.

catusaṭṭhikkhattuṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Number adverb formed from catusaṭṭhi (64) and khattuṃ (times). Occurs in Apadāna verses describing the rewards of merit.

kappeto.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text kappeto is a sandhi form of kappeti (etymologically kappayati); the following satasahasse is the object. Third person singular present of the causative of √kapp.
kappeto.example_1: Gotamo nāma gottena, satthā loke bhavissati [yaṃ vadanti sumedhoti, bhūripaññaṃ sumedhasaṃ; kappeto satasahasse, esa buddho bhavissati;(ka.)].
kappeto.translation_1: called Gotama by clan, will be the Teacher in the world.

pasobhito.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it describes an elephant adorned with a white umbrella, etc. pp of pasobhati; nominative singular in -o.
pasobhito.translation_2: Adorned with a white umbrella, with trappings and a mahout,

sahatthipo.meaning_2: together with the elephant; accompanied by elephants; with a mahout
sahatthipo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Descriptive compound used of a horse or vehicle; the PEU explains hatthipa as 'one who protects elephants', here in the sense of elephants or a mahout. Nominative singular in the text.
sahatthipo.translation_2: Adorned with a white umbrella, with trappings and a mahout,

dasañcaṭṭhakkhatthuṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of dasa + ca + aṭṭha + kkhattuṃ (\'ten and eight times\'), a gloss on the Dasa aṭṭha of the preceding line; variant dasa caṭṭhakkhattuṃ. The sandhi reading treats it as dasa + ca + aṭṭha + kkhattuṃ rather than dasa + aṭṭha + kkhattuṃ, giving \'ten and eight times\' i.e. eighteen times. Indeclinable numeral phrase used adverbially; the cc- is the sandhi of ca + aṭṭha.
dasañcaṭṭhakkhatthuṃ.example_1: 137. ‘‘‘ Dasa aṭṭha cakkhattuṃ [dasañcaṭṭhakkhatthuṃ (sī.), dasa caṭṭhakkhattuṃ (syā.)] so, cakkavattī bhavissati;
dasañcaṭṭhakkhatthuṃ.translation_1: Eighteen times he will be a Wheel-turning Monarch.

caṭṭhakkhattuṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading of aṭṭhakkhattuṃ (cf. dasa aṭṭha cakkhattuṃ); the text's caṭṭhakkhattuṃ is a sandhi of ca + aṭṭhakkhattuṃ, where ca belongs to the preceding dasa. Meaning 'eighteen times' in the verse.
caṭṭhakkhattuṃ.example_1: 137. ‘‘‘ Dasa aṭṭha cakkhattuṃ [dasañcaṭṭhakkhatthuṃ (sī.), dasa caṭṭhakkhattuṃ (syā.)] so, cakkavattī bhavissati;
caṭṭhakkhattuṃ.translation_1: Eighteen times he will be a Wheel-turning Monarch.
caṭṭhakkhattuṃ.example_2: 53. ‘‘‘ Dasa aṭṭha cakkhattuṃ [dasa caṭṭhakkhattuṃ (sī.), dasamaṭṭhakkhattuṃ (syā.)] so, devarajjaṃ karissati;
caṭṭhakkhattuṃ.translation_2: “For ten and eight times he will exercise divine rule.

yārissati.meaning_2: you will not be invited; nowhere will you be invited
yārissati.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of yā (probably a corruption of yaṃ or yā + assa) and ārissati, future of ārādhayati (invite; satisfy) with na: 'nowhere will you be pleased/invited'. The text reads yārissati; the meaning given in the sentence is based on the future of ārādhayati. The reading is uncertain (syā. notes it).
yārissati.example_1: Tathā sīlavihīno tvaṃ, na jhāyissasi [yārissati (syā.)] katthaci.
yārissati.translation_1: so you, without moral restraint, won’t be invited anywhere.

dammito.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text dammito is a variant reading for dappito; nominative singular describing an elephant-king. It is a past participle of dameti, used adjectivally.

abbhuggamī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 3rd singular of abbhuggamati (abhi + u + √gam), used of the hero flying into the sky (nabhaṃ). Also spelt abbhuggañchi/abbhuggami; abbhuggamī is the form metrically lengthened before a break.

ālagetvāna.meaning_2: having attached; having stuck (to); having tied (onto)
ālagetvāna.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive in -tvāna of the causative ālageti (ā + √lag + *e), 'to cause to stick, attach'. In the sentence it governs veḷagge, 'having attached (it) to the bamboo pole'. The PEU split Ā+laga+tvāna agrees.
ālagetvāna.translation_1: stuck it onto a bamboo pole, and raised a flag into the sky.

ussīsanti.meaning_2: is raised; stands up; is displayed
ussīsanti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The DPD text reads ussīsanti, which appears to be a sandhi of ussīsanti (3rd plural passive of ussīsati) or a variant of ussīyanti; if the latter, see ussīyati. The meaning is uncertain.
ussīsanti.translation_2: flags were always seen by me for three leagues in all directions.

gopayiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 1st singular of the causative gopeti. In the text it takes the object paripuṇṇāni sīlāni. The PEU split gupa+ṇaya is uncertain.

agopayiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 1st person singular of gopeti (causative of √gup). The first word, agopayiṃ, with paripuṇṇaṃ means 'I guarded completely'. Sometimes analysed as gopayiṃ in sandhi with na, but here the aorist fits.
agopayiṃ.translation_2: For all that time, I guarded the refuge-going completely.

upasampādayi.meaning_2: ordains; admits (into the Saṅgha); causes to attain
upasampādayi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 3rd singular upasampādayi in the text, used of the Buddha ordaining the speaker. Causative of upasampajjati; sometimes analysed as upa + saṃ + pada + ṇaya.
upasampādayi.translation_2: Knowing my virtue, the Eyeful One, the Buddha, ordained me.

suppaṇīhitaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In mānasaṃ suppaṇīhitaṃ, mānasaṃ is an adjective meaning 'well-aimed; well-directed'. This form is a past participle of suppaṇidahati, 'to place or apply well', with the su- prefix. The text shows it in the accusative singular neuter, agreeing with mānasaṃ. 'Pṇī' is the sandhi form of 'pani'.
suppaṇīhitaṃ.translation_2: 125. “Well-protected was my refuge, my mind well-placed.

parigopiya.meaning_2: having protected; having guarded; having preserved
parigopiya.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive in -iya of the causative parigopeti (cf. parigopāya, parigopāyaṃ). In the text it governs sīlāni: 'guarding the virtues'.
parigopiya.example_2: 130. ‘‘‘ Sammā dhammaṃ bhāvetvāna [mamopamaṃ karitvāna (sī. syā.)], sīlāni parigopiya;
parigopiya.translation_2: 130. “Rightly developing the Dhamma, guarding your virtues,

pañcasīlasamādāniyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of the elder who undertook the five precepts; title of the fourth chapter of the Apadāna
pañcasīlasamādāniyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A title heading, nominative singular in the text. The compound is pañca + sīla + samādāniya + thera + apadāna, with the last two members joined by sandhi (tt).

saṃkittento.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Present participle (causative) used in the text to describe proclaiming the manly deed. Alternative forms pakittenta in some editions.
saṃkittento.example_1: 150. ‘‘ Saṃkittento ca [pakittentova (sī.), pakittente ca (syā.)] sabbesaṃ, abhimattañca porisaṃ;
saṃkittento.translation_1: Proclaiming this outstanding human action to everyone,

abhimattañca.meaning_2: and the overpowered man; and the overcome person
abhimattañca.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text the string is printed as abhimattañca = abhimattaṃ + ca in sandhi; the ending is not a grammatical case of a single word. The reading and translation are from the given text.
abhimattañca.example_1: 150. ‘‘ Saṃkittento ca [pakittentova (sī.), pakittente ca (syā.)] sabbesaṃ, abhimattañca porisaṃ;
abhimattañca.translation_1: Proclaiming this outstanding human action to everyone,

annasaṃsāvakattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of the elder who announced the food; name of a chapter of the Apadāna
annasaṃsāvakattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title heading of an Apadāna chapter; nominative singular in -ṃ. Contains the name Annasaṃsāvaka.

abhināmetvā.meaning_2: having bent towards; having inclined; having brought (near); having directed (towards)
abhināmetvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative absolutive of abhināmeti (abhi + √nam, caus). In the verse it describes respectfully directing or bringing the Buddha forward, hence 'having invited, having brought near'.
abhināmetvā.translation_2: 157. Having invited the Sambuddha, I fed that great sage;

abhirūhi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 3rd singular in the verse, referring to the Great Sage mounting (the throne). Could also be read as an imperative 'climb up', but the narrative context favours the aorist.
abhirūhi.translation_2: 173. Having heard my loud growling, the Great Sage climbed aboard.

ekañjalimakāsahaṃ.meaning_2: I paid homage with a single añjali; I pressed the palms together once (in respect)
ekañjalimakāsahaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Analysis uncertain. Best taken as sandhi resolving to ekaṃ añjaliṃ akāsiṃ ahaṃ (the -s- of akāsaṃ being a sandhi variant of akāsiṃ), i.e. 'I made a single añjali'. Alternatively eka + añjali + aka + āsahaṃ ('I performed a single añjali'). Occurs at the end of a verse, so metre may explain the form.
ekañjalimakāsahaṃ.translation_2: On seeing him, pleased and with happiness of mind, I pressed my hands together once.

pañcālīsītisataṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Number (the number of verses), nominative singular in the text. The first part is sandhi of pañca + cattaḷīsa (> pañcālīsa); cf. pañcacattālīsasata.
pañcālīsītisataṃ.translation_1: One hundred and eighty-five verses have been spoken, all gathered together.

kadalīkaṇṇiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text. Second member kaṇṇi (from kaṇṇikā, "ear, stalk") loses its ending for the metre; some editions read kadalīkaṇṇikaṃ. Meaning per PEU: a bunch of bananas.
kadalīkaṇṇiṃ.translation_2: I approached him, carrying a large sheaf of banana fruits.

ekādasañcakkhattuṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of ekādasaṃ + cakkhattuṃ (the ṃ becomes ñ before c). Alternative reading in the text is ekādasakkhattuṃ. Used adverbially to mean 'eleven times'.
ekādasañcakkhattuṃ.translation_2: He will be a king of gods for eleven times,

gāhayī.meaning_2: causes to take; has (someone) take; makes take; hands over
gāhayī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative of gaṇhāti used with salākaṃ (ticket) in the Apadāna verses: 'the Victor had (me) take the ticket'. The form gāhayī is the aorist 3rd singular.
gāhayī.translation_2: the Victor sat in the Saṅgha of bhikkhus and had me take a ticket.

dasamaṭṭhakkhattuṃ.meaning_2: ten and eight times; eighteen times
dasamaṭṭhakkhattuṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of dasa + aṭṭha + kkhattuṃ (aṭṭha + kkhattuṃ with consonant doubling). Variant readings: caṭṭhakkhattuṃ and aṭṭhakkhattuṃ in other editions; the sense is 'for ten and eight times'.
dasamaṭṭhakkhattuṃ.example_1: 53. ‘‘‘ Dasa aṭṭha cakkhattuṃ [dasa caṭṭhakkhattuṃ (sī.), dasamaṭṭhakkhattuṃ (syā.)] so, devarajjaṃ karissati;
dasamaṭṭhakkhattuṃ.translation_1: “For ten and eight times he will exercise divine rule.

cakkhūsi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A short form of cakkhumant in a compound, used in the sense of 'one who is the eye for' others. Nominative singular in the text.
cakkhūsi.translation_2: You are the eye for all, the dispeller of great darkness.

udakehaṃ.meaning_2: I (do not die) in water; in the water I
udakehaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of udake (locative singular of udaka) + ahaṃ. In the text it means 'I (do not die) in the water'.
udakehaṃ.example_2: Udakehaṃ na miyyāmi, āyāgassa idaṃ phalaṃ.
udakehaṃ.translation_2: I do not die in water; this is the fruit of an eating hall.

tisakkhattuṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Adverb of number; ti + sakkhattuṃ. In the text it modifies ahosiṃ.
tisakkhattuṃ.translation_1: I was a wheel-turning monarch, possessing the seven gems, thirty times;

dhammacakkikattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of the Elder Dhammacakkika; the Apadāna of the Elder Dhammacakkika
dhammacakkikattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of the ninth chapter of the Thera-Apadāna. Nominative singular in the text; dissimilation gives -tt-.

dhammacakkikattherassāpadānaṃ.meaning_2: the Apadāna of the Elder Dhammacakkika
dhammacakkikattherassāpadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of the ninth chapter. Sandhi of the genitive dhammacakkikattherassa and the nominative apadānaṃ; the compound on its own is dhammacakkika + thera.

lasuṇado.meaning_2: garlic giver; donor of garlic; name of a Paccekabuddha
lasuṇado.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A name (proper noun) in the Apadāna list of Paccekabuddhas, also analysable as an epithet 'giver of garlic' (lasuṇa + da from √dā). Nominative singular in the text.

kapparukkhī.meaning_2: name of a monk; the Elder Kapparukkhiya
kapparukkhī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name of a Thera, apparently formed from kapparukkha + -iya and listed as the tenth (dasamo) in the Apadāna. The form in the text is nominative singular.
kapparukkhī.example_2: Kapparukkhī ca dasamo, gāthā dvayadasasataṃ [gāthāyo dvādasasataṃ (sī.)].
kapparukkhī.translation_2: Kapparukkhī is the tenth; one hundred and twelve verses.

paṭisallituṃ.meaning_2: to go into seclusion; to retire to a quiet place
paṭisallituṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Infinitive used with gacchate, 'goes to seclusion'. From paṭisallīyati (paṭi + saṃ + √lī).
paṭisallituṃ.translation_2: being one bound to solitude, went off into seclusion.

anileritaaṅgaṇamhi.meaning_2: a place free from stirred-up dust; an unswept courtyard
anileritaaṅgaṇamhi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Locative singular in the text. anilerita = not stirred up (by the wind); aṅgaṇa = open space, courtyard.
anileritaaṅgaṇamhi.translation_2: “When the rain has fallen four inches, on grass in a dust-free place,

supaṇīhitaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Past participle with intensive prefix su- (well). Accusative singular neuter modifying cittaṃ in the text. Sanskrit supraṇihita. The PEU entry suggests the same split.
supaṇīhitaṃ.example_2: 51. ‘‘ Uttame damathe danto, cittaṃ me supaṇīhitaṃ;
supaṇīhitaṃ.translation_2: “Tamed in the ultimate taming, my mind is well-directed;

abhināmayiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] 1st person singular aorist of the causative abhināmayati (√nam + *aya), meaning 'I brought/led towards'. In the text, it takes the object saṅgharaṃ ('house').
abhināmayiṃ.translation_2: with a pleased heart and happy mind, I led him into my house.

sannidhāpako.meaning_2: one who causes to acquire; one who stores up; one who provides
sannidhāpako.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Name of a thero (Sanniṭṭhāpako in the Burmese edition) in the concluding line of this Apadāna; nominative singular in the text.
sannidhāpako.example_1: Itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā sanniṭṭhāpako [sannidhāpako (sī.)] thero imā gāthāyo abhāsitthāti.
sannidhāpako.translation_1: Thus indeed the venerable Sanniṭṭhāpaka Thera spoke these verses.

uggamī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 3rd singular of uggamati (ud + √gam), used of the Buddha flying up into the air. Some editions read uggamī ti with a following ti.
uggamī.example_2: Uṭṭhāya sayanā [āsanā (sī.)] tamhā, vehāsaṃ uggamī jino.
uggamī.translation_2: Having risen from that seat, the Victor flew up into the air.

bodhayitvā.meaning_2: having awakened; having enlightened; having made known
bodhayitvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative absolutive of bodheti. In the text it is part of the phrase bodhayitvā bahū satte.
bodhayitvā.translation_2: the one with vision, having awakened many beings, will attain final nibbāna.

sopagato.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of so (pronoun) + upagato (pp of upagacchati). Occurs in the Apadāna verse.
sopagato.translation_2: At that time, he, having approached, being incited by wholesome roots,

pupphagghiyamupānayiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of pupphagghiyaṃ (accusative singular of pupphagghiya, 'flower garland') and upānayiṃ (aorist 1st singular of upānayati, 'brought; offered'). The -ṃ becomes -m before the vowel. In the text the speaker is the offering devotee.
pupphagghiyamupānayiṃ.translation_2: with a pleased mind and feeling happy, I offered that floral festoon work.

vivatthacchaddo.meaning_2: with the covering removed; whose cover is open
vivatthacchaddo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The text's vivatthacchaddo is a variant spelling of vivaṭṭacchado (second t, doubled dd); nominative singular here, an epithet of the Buddha. The first element may also be analysed as vi + vaṭṭa, 'unrolled, uncovered'.
vivatthacchaddo.translation_1: the Sambuddha with the covering removed, will arise at that time.

gandhodakiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of the Elder Gandhodakiya; Gandhodakiya Thera's Apadāna
gandhodakiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of the fourth chapter of the Apadāna. Nominative singular in the text.

gandhodakiyattherassāpadānaṃ.meaning_2: the story of the Elder Gandhodakiya; Gandhodakiya's Apadāna
gandhodakiyattherassāpadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of the fourth Apadāna of the Gandhodakiya chapter. Nominative singular in the text, the headword is given as the compound stem.

asanabodhiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the Apadāna (legend) of the Elder Asanabodhiya; title of the tenth chapter of the Therāpadāna
asanabodhiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A text title in the Apadāna, nominative singular in the heading. Probably Asana + bodhiya ('awakened under the asana tree'), but the thera's name could also be analysed as asana + bodhi + ya.
asanabodhiyattheraapadānaṃ.translation_1: The legend of Asanabodhiya Thera, the tenth.

ropayiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 1st person singular of the causative ropeti (< √ruh).

avopupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of Āvopupphiya Thera; the story of the elder Avopupphiya
avopupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title heading of an Apadāna chapter. Nominative singular in the text. Proper name of the elder is Āvopupphiya.

avopupphiyattherassāpadānaṃ.meaning_2: the Apadāna (legend) of the Elder Avopupphiya; Avopupphiya's Apadāna
avopupphiyattherassāpadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of avopupphiyattherassa + apadānaṃ; the title closing the second Apadāna. Avopupphiya is the name of the elder (possibly ava + uppupphiya, 'down-flowered'), therassa is genitive singular, apadānaṃ nominative neuter singular.

sindhuyā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Name of a river; genitive singular sindhuyā in the text, in the phrase sindhuyā nadiyā tīre (on the bank of the Sindhu river).
sindhuyā.example_2: 13. ‘‘ Sindhuyā nadiyā tīre, cakkavāko ahaṃ tadā;
sindhuyā.translation_2: Back then, I was a ruddy goose on the bank of the Indus River;

susumpattiṃ.meaning_2: great success; high prosperity; excellent good fortune
susumpattiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The text reads susumpattiṃ, a variant spelling of susampattiṃ (cf. the sī. and syā. readings), accusative singular; the second verse has sukhasampattiṃ parallel to it.
susumpattiṃ.translation_1: I’ve come to know no bad rebirth (duggatiṃ): that is the fruit (phalaṃ) of praising him. I enjoyed no small quantity of happiness in good rebirths (sugatiṃ).

pupphacaṅkoṭiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of the Elder Pupphacaṅkoṭiya; Pupphacaṅkoṭiya Thera's apadāna
pupphacaṅkoṭiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of the tenth chapter of the Thera-apadāna; nominative singular in the text. It is the name of the chapter, not an ordinary noun.

pupphacaṅkoṭiyo.meaning_2: name of a monk (the Elder Pupphacaṅkoṭiya)
pupphacaṅkoṭiyo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Name of a Thera, probably "(one who kept) flowers in a basket" (puppha + caṅkoṭi + ya). Nominative singular in the text; the same word appears as a proper noun in the Apadāna.
pupphacaṅkoṭiyo.example_1: itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā pupphacaṅkoṭiyo thero imā gāthāyo abhāsitthāti.

pupphacaṅkoṭiyattherassāpadānaṃ.meaning_2: the Elder Pupphacaṅkoṭiya's Apadāna (legend); the tenth (chapter)
pupphacaṅkoṭiyattherassāpadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title line concluding the chapter. Pupphacaṅkoṭiyattherassa is the genitive singular of the elder's name plus apadānaṃ, the nominative/accusative singular; the whole is a minor sandhi. Sometimes analysed as one compound.

avopupphī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] This is a sandhi compound of saka + cintī? The entry is for the first word of the verse, not avopupphī.

parappasādī.meaning_2: who gladdens others; making others confident; inspiring faith in others
parappasādī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Possessive (bahubbīhi) compound with -ī suffix: 'whose serene confidence is (produced) in others' or 'producing faith in others'. Used as an epithet or name in a list of names in the Apadāna.

bhisado.meaning_2: name of a Pacceka Buddha; name of a previous Buddha
bhisado.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name occurring in the Apadāna list of Pacceka Buddhas; nominative singular in the text. The elements are uncertain: possibly bhisa (lotus root) + da, or related to bhisadāna.

pupphacaṅkoṭakīpi.meaning_2: name of an arahant; the one with a flower-basket (previous birth name)
pupphacaṅkoṭakīpi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name in the Apadāna list of eminent disciples; -pi of the text is the enclitic, omitted here. The Peu token pupphacaṅkoṭaka (masc) means flower basket; the name is presumably from a previous birth connected with a basket of flowers.
pupphacaṅkoṭakīpi.translation_2: Ambadāyī and Sumano, and also Pupphacaṅkoṭakī,

bhisāluvañca.meaning_2: edible lotus roots and tubers; (or) edible roots and yams
bhisāluvañca.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A compound of bhisa (edible lotus root) and āluva (edible tuber); the text has bhisāluvaṃ, accusative singular, with -ca (and) appended. Āluva is masculine; compound may be neuter.
bhisāluvañca.translation_2: 14. I gave him edible roots and water to wash his hands.

pāṭalipupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of the Elder Pāṭalipupphiya; Pāṭalipupphiya Thera's Apadāna
pāṭalipupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title heading at the start of the Thera's Apadāna. Nominative singular in -ṃ. The first element pāṭalipupphiya means 'one who offered pāṭali flowers'.

ṭhitañjaliyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of the Elder Ṭhitañjali; Ṭhitañjaliya Thera's apadāna
ṭhitañjaliyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of the ninth chapter of the Thera-apadāna. Probably a dvandva-type title compound (ṭhitañjaliya + thera + apadāna), though it may be read as Ṭhitañjaliya + therāpadānaṃ; given as one word in the text.

tipadumiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of Tipadumīya Thera; the Apadāna of the Elder Tipadumīya
tipadumiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A text title heading a chapter of the Apadāna. Nominative singular in the text. The thera's name is spelled tipadumī in the lemma but tipadumiya- in the compound.

toṇi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Found in the Apadāna verse 'uttamaṃ toṇi ... aggahiṃ'. The word is otherwise unattested; the PEU suggests a connection with toṇḍi (Tamil region), which does not fit the context. Probably a flower term; the edition may vary (cf. pupphaṃ).
toṇi.example_1: Yaṃ tattha uttamaṃ toṇi, padmapupphāni [uttamaṃ pupphaṃ, tīṇi pupphāni (sī.)] aggahiṃ.
toṇi.translation_1: I picked up three flower-blossoms which were the foremost flowers there.

upanitehi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Past participle of upaneti, used in the instrumental plural upanitehi, agreeing with the speaker: 'offered by me to the king'. Part of the phrase rañño upanitehi me.
upanitehi.example_2: 51. ‘‘ Kiṃ me imehi pupphehi, rañño upanitehi me;
upanitehi.translation_2: “What use are these flowers to me even if gifted to a king?

sampavattayuṃ.meaning_2: caused to arise; set in motion; produced; (or) arose; occurred
sampavattayuṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 3rd plural form sampavattayuṃ; caus of sampavattati, from √vatt with *e. Alternative analysis as simple aorist of sampavattati (they occurred).
sampavattayuṃ.example_2: 55. ‘‘ Ye keci manujā disvā, ukkuṭṭhiṃ sampavattayuṃ;
sampavattayuṃ.translation_2: Whatever people saw them there then kept them thrown up in the air

tipadumānidaṃ.meaning_2: this (is) the fruit of three lotuses; this fruit of three lotuses
tipadumānidaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of tipadumānaṃ (genitive plural of tipaduma, 'of three lotuses') + idaṃ ('this'), with the final ṃ becoming n before the vowel. The whole phrase tipadumānidaṃ phalaṃ means 'this is the fruit of three lotuses'. Alternative resolution tipadumāna + idaṃ is less likely.
tipadumānidaṃ.translation_2: I’ve come to know no bad rebirth: that’s the fruit of three lotuses.

tipadumiyattherassāpadānaṃ.meaning_2: the Apadāna (chapter) on the Elder Tipadumiya (sutta); the sutta of the Elder Tipadumiya's Apadāna
tipadumiyattherassāpadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] It is a compound. Text reads tipadumiyattherassāpadānaṃ dasamaṃ. It is an editorial heading (the tenth sutta) and the compound contains the genitive therassa. It is declined as an a-stem nt; for the nominative singular, note the final -ṃ in the text.

tipadumī.meaning_2: Tipadumī; (the elder) connected with three lotuses
tipadumī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Name of a Thera in the Apadāna, occurring in the verse-title Ṭhitañjalī tipadumī. Probably short for tipadumiya. Could also be read as a feminine name.
tipadumī.translation_2: Ṭhitañjalī, Tipadumī: five and seventy verses.

timirapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of Timirapupphiya Thera; Timirapupphiya Thera's Apadāna
timirapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title heading of a chapter of the Apadāna, nominative singular; timira means 'darkness' and pupphiya is the monk's name.

adhopupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of the Elder Adhopupphiya
adhopupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title heading in the text; nominative singular in -aṃ. Adhopupphiya is the name of the elder.
adhopupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.translation_1: The Legend of the Thera Adhopupphiya.

abhimatthayiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 1st singular in the text; variant reading abhimatthayiṃ; possibly from abhimattheti, causative of mattheti. Meaning in context is doubtful; see PEU abhimatthati (tortured, crushed).
abhimatthayiṃ.example_1: 24. ‘‘ Pakkhijāto viyākāse, pabbataṃ adhivattayiṃ [abhipatthayiṃ (syā.), abhimatthayiṃ (ka.), adhivatthayinti pabbatassa upari gacchintiattho];
abhimatthayiṃ.translation_1: Like a bird in the sky, I moved towards the mountain;

adhivatthayinti.meaning_2: went over; moved towards; went above
adhivatthayinti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Found as adhivatthayinti, likely adhivattayiṃ + iti, or an orthographic variant in the edition; the commentary glosses as 'went above the mountain'. First person singular aorist in the text.
adhivatthayinti.example_1: 24. ‘‘ Pakkhijāto viyākāse, pabbataṃ adhivattayiṃ [abhipatthayiṃ (syā.), abhimatthayiṃ (ka.), adhivatthayinti pabbatassa upari gacchintiattho];
adhivatthayinti.translation_1: Like a bird in the sky, I moved towards the mountain;

bodhimabhisiñcayiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Here in the sandhi bodhimabhisiñcayiṃ = bodhiṃ + abhisiñcayiṃ; the simplex siñcati means to sprinkle, and abhisiñcati (often used of honouring or anointing) is glossed in the commentary tradition as watering the Bodhi Tree. 1st person singular aorist.
bodhimabhisiñcayiṃ.translation_2: In the ninety-one aeons since, when I watered that Bodhi Tree,

padumapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of the Elder Padumapupphiya; Padumapupphiya Thera's Apadāna
padumapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of a chapter in the Apadāna. Nominative singular in the text. The stems paduma and pupphiya are doubtful; padumapupphiya means 'one who offered a lotus flower'.

aṭṭhatālīsamāsisuṃ.meaning_2: forty-eight (monarchs) they were; there were forty-eight
aṭṭhatālīsamāsisuṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aṭṭhatālīsaṃ + āsisuṃ (aorist of atthi, 'they were'). 3rd plural aorist in the text, describing forty-eight kings in the eighteenth aeon.
aṭṭhatālīsamāsisuṃ.translation_2: and in the eighteenth aeon there were forty-eight such monarchs.

timiranaṅgalīpuppha.meaning_2: flower of the timira and naṅgalī plants; timira-naṅgalī flower
timiranaṅgalīpuppha.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A list of flower names in the Apadāna verse; vocative in the text. Possibly two separate words, timira and naṅgalīpuppha, in the list.

phalado.meaning_2: provider of fruit; fruit-giver; name of a paccekabuddha
phalado.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the verse it names a paccekabuddha (nominative singular phalado). It can also be read as a compound meaning 'fruit-giver' (phala + dā).

secako.meaning_2: name of a monk; sprinkler; pourer
secako.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name of a Paccekabuddha (or monk) in the Apadāna list. Nominative singular in the text.
secako.example_2: Dve raṃsisaññī phalado, saddasaññī ca secako;
secako.translation_2: two Raṃsisaññīs, Phalada, Saddasaññī, and Secaka,

sudhāpiṇḍiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of the elder Sudhāpiṇḍiya; the life story of venerable Sudhāpiṇḍiya
sudhāpiṇḍiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of a Theragāthā-apadāna chapter. Sandhi: thera + apadāna → theraapadāna. The elder's name is sudhāpiṇḍiya (one who had a lump of gruel?), here in compound form. Nominative singular in the text.

idammattanti.meaning_2: ‘it is only this much’ (said); ‘just this amount’
idammattanti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of idaṃ + mattaṃ + iti; alternative reading imetthamapi. Used in the phrase imettamapi kenaci, ‘it is only this much’.
idammattanti.example_1: Na sakkā puññaṃ saṅkhātuṃ, imettamapi [idammattanti (sī.), imetthamapi (ka.)] kenaci.
idammattanti.translation_1: no one can count the merit, saying 'it is this much'.

uparuci.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name of a king in a list of kings. Nominative singular. Possibly a compound with upa (cf. uparāja), but the second element is a name. Not declined in the text.
uparuci.translation_2: Ruci and Uparuci, and Mahāruci was the third.

nibbūtikaṃ.meaning_2: with fire extinguished; with (the fires) quenched
nibbūtikaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading (syā.) for nibbutattaṃ in the text; accusative singular agreeing with mahānāgaṃ. Probably a derivative of nibbuta.
nibbūtikaṃ.translation_1: the one whose fires are extinguished, the Great Elephant, like a thoroughbred bull,

tuvaṭṭāmi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] 1st person singular present in the text (tuvaṭṭāmi), meaning 'I lie down'. The root √tuvaṭṭ (also given as √tuvaṭṭ in the DPD root list, 'lie down') is rare and mostly confined to verse.
tuvaṭṭāmi.translation_2: 47. I lie down on my bed, on an ornamented mat of flowers;

veyyāvaccakattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of the Elder Veyyāvaccaka; Veyyāvaccakattheraapadāna (title of a chapter)
veyyāvaccakattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title heading of the ninth chapter of the Apadāna. Nominative singular in -aṃ; sandhi has merged the final -a of thera with the initial a- of apadāna.

muṭṭhipupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of the Elder Muṭṭhipupphiya; title of the fifth chapter of the Apadāna
muṭṭhipupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A text title; nominative singular in the heading. The elder is named after a flower held in the fist (muṭṭhi + puppha). Printed with 'tt' by sandhi.

bījitvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading of bandhitvā and bījitvā in the same line; the fan is 'fanned' here. The root √vīj (fan) becomes bīja- with loss of the vowel.
bījitvā.translation_1: Taking a garland of reeds, I bound it into a fan;

āsanupaṭṭhāhakattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of the Elder who attended to seats; title of the eighth chapter of the Apadāna
āsanupaṭṭhāhakattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A chapter title in the Apadāna, given as a heading in the text. Nominative singular in -ṃ.

kalambāni.meaning_2: water creeper (a water convolvulus); a kind of edible plant (roots of which are dug up)
kalambāni.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Neuter plural in the text (kalambāni), listed with other edible roots; probably a variant of kalambaka. Possibly a-stem neuter rather than masculine.
kalambāni.translation_2: Digging up roots like kaḷamba, biḷāli, and takkaḷi too,

biḷālitakkalāni.meaning_2: biḷāli and takkala roots; various edible roots (biḷāli and takkala)
biḷālitakkalāni.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative plural of a compound of plant/root names, object of khaṇantālu (khaṇanti); the reading is uncertain, perhaps biḷāli and takkala (or takkala) roots. Recorded only in this verse.
biḷālitakkalāni.translation_2: Digging up roots like kaḷamba, biḷāli, and takkaḷi too,

udakado.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name of a monk in the Apadāna. Nominative singular in the text.

ekāsaniyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of the Elder Ekāsaniya
ekāsaniyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title heading in the Apadāna; nominative singular in the text. ekāsaniya is the name of the thera ("one-seated"), thera the elder, apadāna the legend.

upaṭṭhiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] First person singular aorist; the text also has upaṭṭhiṃ, which can be 3rd singular or 1st singular.

suvaṇṇapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of Suvaṇṇapupphiya Thera; the life story of the venerable Suvaṇṇapupphiya
suvaṇṇapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of section 5 of the Apadāna. In the text it is the nominative singular, used as a heading. The name suvaṇṇapupphiya means 'golden-flower' (or 'one who offered golden flowers'); thera is 'venerable, elder'.

tetālīse.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Locative singular in the text (tetālīse kappe: in the forty-third aeon). Ordinal formed from ti (three) + cattālīsa (forty).
tetālīse.translation_2: in the forty-third aeon before this, Wheel-turning Monarchs with great strength.

citapūjī.meaning_2: honouring the funeral pyre; worshipping the pyre
citapūjī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A bahubbīhi compound. In the text it is a nominative singular used as an epithet. Literally 'pyre-worshipping' (cita + pūjī; cf. citapūjā).

sereyyavaggo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of the thirteenth chapter of the Apadāna. Nominative singular in the text. Sereyya is likely the name of the elder after whom the chapter is named.

sereyyakattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of Sereyyaka Thera; the Apadāna of the elder Sereyyaka
sereyyakattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of a chapter of the Apadāna. Nominative singular in the text (the -ṃ of the title). Sereyyaka is the name of the elder.

sereyyakaṃ.meaning_2: Sereyyaka flower; a flower of the Barleria species
sereyyakaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text. A flower name; probably derived from sereyya, but the exact formation is uncertain.
sereyyakaṃ.translation_2: Having taken up a Sereyyaka flower, I threw it up into the air.

vilāmālā.meaning_2: with a garland of desire; wearing a garland of longing
vilāmālā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading for cittamālā in the text; a bahubbi compound describing the cakkavattī kings. Perhaps vilā (desire) + mālā (garland).
vilāmālā.example_1: Vītamalā [cittamālā (sī.), vilāmālā (syā.)] samānā ca, cakkavattī mahabbalā.
vilāmālā.translation_1: Vītamala by name, wheel-turning monarchs with great strength.

sereyyako.meaning_2: name of an elder; name of a monk
sereyyako.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Name of a thera, the speaker of these verses in the Apadāna.
sereyyako.example_1: itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā sereyyako thero imā gāthāyo abhāsitthāti.

sereyyakattherassāpadānaṃ.meaning_2: the Apadāna of the Elder Sereyya
sereyyakattherassāpadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A title in the Apadāna; nominative singular in the text.

vāsayituṃ.meaning_2: to stay; to live; to dwell
vāsayituṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Infinitive of the causative vāsayati (to make stay, to lodge; here simply to stay). Used with gamiṃ (went) in the text: 'I went to stay'. The PEU splits it as vasa + ṇaya + tuṃ.
vāsayituṃ.example_2: Byādhinā pīḷito santo, sālaṃ vāsayituṃ gamiṃ.
vāsayituṃ.translation_2: Being afflicted by that illness, I went to stay beneath a sal tree.

saṃcari.meaning_2: moves about; roams; circulates; moves together
saṃcari.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 3rd singular in the text (saṃcari). The pey entry reads it as present saṃcarati; the sentence requires a past tense.
saṃcari.translation_1: 46. “And when that one was being born, the flocks of birds did not move;

vilokayi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 3rd singular of viloketi (causative of vilokati). The form vilokayi is used in the verse. Alternative analysis: aorist of vilokayati.
vilokayi.example_2: 50. ‘‘‘ Jātamatto ca sambuddho, disā sabbā vilokayi;
vilokayi.translation_2: 50. “And when the Sambuddha was born, he looked in all directions;

saṃvejayitvā.meaning_2: having stirred; having moved; having roused; having inspired
saṃvejayitvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Form of saṃvejeti (causative of saṃvijati, √vij). Absolutive in -tvā used in verse; the readings saṃvejayitvā and saṃvejetvā both occur.
saṃvejayitvā.translation_2: 51. “Having moved the generations, and having praised the Leader of the World,

duddasi.meaning_2: name of a previous Buddha; hard to see
duddasi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading in the text, with the main reading Pathavīdundubhi. The commentary glosses it as a name (duddasi nāma). Perhaps a miswriting of duddasa or duddasī; the meaning 'hard to see' is doubtful here. Nominative singular.
duddasi.translation_1: 54. “In the eighty-ninth aeon before this, Pathavīdundubhi by name,

agginibbāpano.meaning_2: name of a Buddha (lit. extinguishing the fire)
agginibbāpano.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Name of a past Buddha. In the text it is nominative singular with the reading agginibbāpano.
agginibbāpano.translation_2: 57. “Agginibbāpana by name, in the eighty-sixth aeon,

vilokano.meaning_2: name of a king; looking at; observing
vilokano.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name of a former king in the Apadāna; nominative singular in the text.
vilokano.translation_2: 62. “The king Vilokana by name, in the eighty-first aeon,

gaṇṭhipupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of the Elder Gaṇṭhipupphiya; title of the ninth chapter of the Apadāna
gaṇṭhipupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A chapter title in the Apadāna. Nominative singular in the text; the final -ṃ is the case ending, not part of the stem.

pupphathūpi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Name of a thera, nominative singular in the text as part of a list of names. Compound of puppha and thūpi (stupa).

āsani.meaning_2: name of a monk (in a list of Paccekabuddhas or previous Buddhas)
āsani.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name in a verse list; the sandhi -i may stand for -ī or -a; not the noun āsana (seat).
āsani.translation_2: Āsani, Phala, and Saññī, Gaṇṭhi, and Padumapupphiya;

abhipūjemi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Causative formed with the suffix ṇe (*e); 1st person singular in the text (abhipūjemi = I revere).
abhipūjemi.translation_2: I revere that knowledge, O Best Buddha, O Great Sage.”

candanapūjanakattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of Candanapūjanaka Thera; the life story of the elder who honoured with sandalwood
candanapūjanakattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of a chapter of the Apadāna. Compound of candana (sandalwood), pūjanaka (honouring), thera (elder) and apadāna (legend). Nominative singular in the text.

rohaṇī.meaning_2: name of a woman; name of a female character (in the Apadāna); (also) name of a female attendant
rohaṇī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name in the Apadāna verse; understood by the commentary as rohitā or rohiṇī. The gender is uncertain; recorded here as feminine.
rohaṇī.example_2: Rohaṇī nāma [rohitā nāma (sī.), rohiṇī nāma (syā.)] nāmena, cakkavattī mahabbalā.
rohaṇī.translation_2: all known by the name Rohiṇi, wheel-turning monarchs with great strength.

campakapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: legend of Campakapupphiya Thera; Campakapupphiya Thera's apadāna
campakapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title heading of the sixth chapter; nominative singular in the text. Campakapupphiya is the name of a thera ('one who offered campaka flowers').

paricāriṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 1st singular of the causative paricāreti (pari + √car). Object vināyakaṃ in the accusative. Some grammars would class this form as imperfect rather than aorist.
paricāriṃ.translation_2: 69. Depending on that, I waited on the Guide;

atichattiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of the Elder Atichattīya; the Apadāna of Atichattīya Thera
atichattiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of a chapter in the Apadāna; nominative singular in the text. The elder's name is otherwise spelled atichattīya.

thūpasīkhasanāmakā.meaning_2: named Thūpasīkha; called Thūpasīkha; whose name was Thūpasīkha
thūpasīkhasanāmakā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Epithet of ninety-four aeons of kings in Apadāna verse 8. Nominative plural in the text (an -ā ending of the plural, not sandhi). PEU analysis thūpasīkha + samāna + nāma + ka is doubtful; possibly thūpasīkha + sanāmaka.
thūpasīkhasanāmakā.translation_2: In the ninety-four aeons since, known by the name Thūpasikha,

umāpupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of the Elder Umāpupphiya; the Apadāna of the Elder Umāpupphiya
umāpupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title heading of the fifth section of the Apadāna. Nominative singular form used as a title; Umāpupphiya is the name of the thera, pupphiya probably 'flowering' from √pupph or a name meaning 'having flowers'.

vaṭaṃsakiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of the elder Vaṭaṃsakiya; the Apadāna of the elder Vaṭaṃsakiya
vaṭaṃsakiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title heading of the ninth Apadāna in the Thera-apadāna, nominative singular in -aṃ as the heading. Vaṭaṃsakiya is a name in -iya from vaṭaṃsaka (garland).
vaṭaṃsakiyattheraapadānaṃ.translation_1: The ninth is the legend of Vaṭaṁsakiyatthera.

ajjhogahi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist-like form ajjhogahi used with present sense here; the prefix adhi + ava > ajjho by sandhi. Sometimes analysed as aorist of ajjhogāhati or as ajjhogāheti (caus).
ajjhogahi.translation_1: strengthening seclusion, entered the great forest.

parivārumapupphiyo.meaning_2: name of a Paccekabuddha (or former Buddha); honoured with an ummā-puppha offering during the Buddha Padumuttara's time
parivārumapupphiyo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Name in a list of Paccekabuddhas in the Apadāna. Nominative singular in the text. The compound is obscure; possibly parivāra + uma-pupphiya 'one who offered an ummā flower as a garland'.
parivārumapupphiyo.example_2: Chattaṃ thambho ca vedi ca, parivārumapupphiyo;
parivārumapupphiyo.translation_2: Chatta, Thambha, and Vedī, Parivāra, Ummapupphiya,

tambapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of the Elder Tambapupphiya; the biography of Tambapupphiya Thera
tambapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of the second apadāna; nominative singular in the text. Tambapupphiya is the elder's name, traditionally 'he who offered copper-coloured flowers'.
tambapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.translation_1: The Legend of the Elder Tambapupphiya

saṃthusito.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading saṃthusito ahuṃ for susaññato ahaṃ; nominative singular describing the king.
saṃthusito.example_1: 13. ‘‘ Ito ca tatiye kappe, rājā susaññato ahaṃ [saṃthusito ahuṃ (sī.)];
saṃthusito.translation_1: In the third aeon before this, I was a king named Susaññata,

vīthisammajjakattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of the Elder Vīthisammajjaka; the story of the Elder Vīthisammajjaka
vīthisammajjakattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of the third chapter of the Vīthisammajjakattheraapadāna in the Apadāna. Nominative singular in -aṃ stands for the whole title; the compound is the name of the text.
vīthisammajjakattheraapadānaṃ.translation_1: 3. The Legend of the Elder Vīthisammajjaka

kadambapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Verse heading (uddāna); nominative singular in -aṃ. Name of the sixth chapter of the Thera-apadāna.
kadambapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.translation_1: The legend of Kadambapupphiya Thera, the sixth (chaṭṭhaṃ).

tiṇasūlakattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of Tiṇasūlaka Thera; the Apadāna of the elder Tiṇasūlaka
tiṇasūlakattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of the seventh chapter of the Apadāna. Nominative singular in the text. The element -ka is a secondary suffix forming the name Tiṇasūlaka.
tiṇasūlakattheraapadānaṃ.translation_1: The legend of Tiṇasūlaka Thera, the seventh (sattamaṃ).

nāgapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of the elder Nāgapupphiya; the Apadāna story of Elder Nāgapupphiya
nāgapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of the eighth Apadāna tale, nominative singular in the text; the compound nāgapupphiya itself is the elder's name (nāga + pupphiya).

punnāgapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of the Elder Punnāgapupphiya; the (text) of Punnāgapupphiya Thera's legend
punnāgapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title heading of a chapter in the Apadāna; nominative singular in the text. Proper name compound of four parts.

kadambī.meaning_2: name of a tree (Nauclea cadamba); kadamba tree
kadambī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Feminine form of kadamba. In these Apadāna verses it appears in a list of trees and is probably a proper name of a tree or a nun's name. Nominative singular.

supāricariyo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name of a monk (thera) in the Apadāna; nominative singular. Sometimes analysed as su + pari + cara + ṇya, 'one who serves well'.
supāricariyo.example_1: itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā supāricariyo thero imā gāthāyo abhāsitthāti.

kaṇaverapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of the Elder Kaṇaverapupphiya; Kaṇaverapupphiya Thera's Apadāna
kaṇaverapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title heading at the start of the chapter; nominative singular in form, though used as a bare title. Kaṇaverapupphiya is the name of the Elder.

desapūjakattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of the Elder Desapūjaka; Desapūjakattheraapadāna
desapūjakattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of the fourth chapter/section of the Apadāna, a compound of desa, pūjaka, thera and apadāna; nominative singular in the text.

kaṇikārachattiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of a section in the Apadāna. Nominative singular in -aṃ.

yūthikapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: legend of the elder Yūthikapupphiya; the Apadāna of the elder Yūthikapupphiya
yūthikapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of the seventh chapter of the Apadāna in the text; nominative singular. Yūthikapupphiya is the elder's epithet ('he who offered a yūthika flower').
yūthikapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.translation_1: The seventh legend of Yūthikapupphiya Thera.

yūthikapupphiyattherassāpadānaṃ.meaning_2: the Apadāna (legend) of the Elder Yūthikapupphiya
yūthikapupphiyattherassāpadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] It is the title of the text, and it appears at the end of the colophon. The form is a sandhi of yūthikapupphiyattherassa, which is the genitive singular of yūthikapupphiyatthera, and apadānaṃ. This is a heading, so it is not declined.

pañcaṅguliyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: legend of Pañcaṅguliya Thera; story of Elder Pañcaṅguliya
pañcaṅguliyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title heading at the end of the Apadāna chapter; nominative singular in the text. Pañcaṅguliya is the thera's name.

supāricari.meaning_2: name of a Pacceka Buddha; Supāricari
supāricari.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A proper name in the Apadāna list of Pacceka Buddhas, in apposition with kaṇaverī in the verse. The spelling with final -i (for -iya, as in supāricariya) is metrical; the PEU takes it as a noun from su + pari + cara + ṇya. Nominative singular in form.
supāricari.translation_2: Supārī and Kaṇaverī, Khujjaka and Desapūjaka,

rattipupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the Apadāna of Rattipupphiya Thera; the legend of the elder Ratti-pupphiya
rattipupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title heading of the third chapter or section of the Apadāna. Ratti-pupphiya probably means 'one who offered a night-flower (ratti-puppha)'. Nominative singular ending -aṃ in the text.

āsayuṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 3rd plural, variant reading of āsu, meaning "there were (eight)". The commentary gloss suggests the reading āsayuṃ; the form is 3rd plural aorist of āsati (√ās, 'sit, be').
āsayuṃ.example_1: 24. ‘‘ Pannarasasahassamhi, kappānaṃ aṭṭha āsu te [aṭṭha āsayuṃ (ka.)];
āsayuṃ.translation_1: In the fifteen-thousandth aeon, there were eight,

ekadīpiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of the Elder Ekadīpiya; Ekadīpiya Thera's Apadāna
ekadīpiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title heading in the Apadāna; nominative singular in the text.

udapānado.meaning_2: name of a deity (Buddha) living in a well; name of a god who lives in a well
udapānado.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A name in a list of deities (Kumuda, Nisseṇī, Rattika, Udapānada). Probably a compound meaning 'one who lives in a well', from udapāna + da, but the etymology is uncertain. Used as a proper name; the same form appears nominative singular and vocative.

maṇippado.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Name of a mountain (probably near the residence Ekadīpī) in the Apadāna. Locative maṇippade. Also analysable as maṇi + pabbata.

kuṭajapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of Kuṭajapupphiya Thera; the story of the elder Kuṭajapupphiya
kuṭajapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of a chapter in the Apadāna. Nominative singular in -ṃ. Kuṭajapupphiya is the name of the elder (thera); the compound is therefore a proper name plus apadāna.

saṃvitthatasamotthataṃ.meaning_2: well spread out and covered (with blossoms); widely expanded and overspread
saṃvitthatasamotthataṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Bahubbīhi compound describing a flowering kuṭaja tree; accusative singular in the text. saṃvitthata = spread out (pp of vi + √thar with saṃ); samotthata = covered, overspread (pp of ava + √thar with saṃ).
saṃvitthatasamotthataṃ.translation_2: On seeing a winter cherry tree, blossoming, well spread out and covered in flowers,

koṭumbariyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of Koṭumbariya Thera; the story of Elder Koṭumbariya
koṭumbariyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of the third chapter of the Apadāna. Nominative singular in the text, written as one sandhi compound.

koṭumbarasamākulaṃ.meaning_2: filled with Koṭumbara blossoms; full of Koṭumbara flowers
koṭumbarasamākulaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it qualifies the flowers being held aloft, so koṭumbara is taken here as a (kind of) flower or blossom rather than the cloth of the PEU gloss. Accusative singular.
koṭumbarasamākulaṃ.translation_2: Lifting up seven flowers, filled with Koṭumbara blossoms,

koṭumbariyattherassāpadānaṃ.meaning_2: the Apadāna (legend) of the Elder Koṭumbariya
koṭumbariyattherassāpadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of the third Apadāna of the Thera chapter. Sandhi of koṭumbariyattherassa (genitive singular of koṭumbariyatthera) + apadānaṃ (nominative singular of apadāna).

buddharaṃsyābhiphuṭṭhomhi.meaning_2: I am touched by the Buddha's rays; I am touched by the light-rays of the Buddha
buddharaṃsyābhiphuṭṭhomhi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The text gives the sandhi of buddha + raṃsīhi (instrumental plural of raṃsi, 'rays') + abhi + phuṭṭha ('touched') + amhi ('I am'); the gloss in the sentence, buddharaṃsīhi phuṭṭhosmi, shows the same sense, though the vowel lengths vary; the variant buddharaṃsābhighuṭṭhosmi is noted in the apparatus.
buddharaṃsyābhiphuṭṭhomhi.translation_1: Touched by the Buddha’s rays, I offered them to the Best Biped.

isimuggadāyakattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of the elder who gave a sickle to the sage; title of the fifth chapter of the Apadāna
isimuggadāyakattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A chapter title in the Apadāna, nominative singular in the text; isi + mugga may also be read as isi + muggadāyaka.
isimuggadāyakattheraapadānaṃ.translation_1: The Legend of Isimuggadāyaka Thera, the fifth.

tikaṇṇipupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of the elder who offered three-ear flowers
