tikaṇṇipupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A chapter or section title in the Apadāna. Nominative singular in the text. The compound is ti + kaṇṇi + pupphiya (perhaps 'three-eared' or 'three-ear-flower') + thera + apadāna.

kiṃkaṇipupphaṃ.meaning_2: kiṅkaṇi flower; kaṇṇi flower (a kind of fragrant flower)
kiṃkaṇipupphaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text. Grammatical variant at verse 47 reads tikaṇṇipupphaṃ; the -ka- variant is accepted here. The first element kiṃkaṇi is a flower name of uncertain analysis.
kiṃkaṇipupphaṃ.translation_1: 47. Lifting up three kaṇṇi flowers, I pleased my own mind;
kiṃkaṇipupphaṃ.translation_2: Lifting up a kiṅkaṇi flower, I offered it to the Buddha;

tikaṇṇipupphiyattherassāpadānaṃ.meaning_2: the Apadāna of the Elder Tikaṇṇipupphiya
tikaṇṇipupphiyattherassāpadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of the eighth Apadāna of the Theras; nominative singular. The compound contains pupphiya, from puppha; the title refers to an offering of three-ears (tikaṇṇi) flowers.

saṅgitaṃ.meaning_2: chanted together; recited in unison; sung
saṅgitaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading for saṅgīti in the verse; here a past participle agreeing with mandāravaṃ. Some editions read saṇhitaṃ.
saṅgitaṃ.translation_1: “Plucking a mandārava bloom, created with magic,

tivaṇṭipupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of Tivaṇṭipupphiya Thera; the Apadāna of the Elder Tivaṇṭipupphiya
tivaṇṭipupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of the tenth chapter of the Apadāna. Nominative singular in the text. The first part is probably ti (three) + vaṇṭi (stalk, stem), with pupphiya from √pupph; the compound as a whole is a title so the root fields are left empty.
tivaṇṭipupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.translation_1: The legend of Tivaṇṭipupphiya Thera, the tenth.

teraseto.meaning_2: from the thirteenth; in the thirteenth (aeon)
teraseto.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of terasa (thirteen) + ito (from here; hence). Used in the phrase teraseto kappasate, meaning 'in the thirteenth aeon from here'. Alternative analysis: terase + ito.
teraseto.translation_2: “In the thirteen hundredth aeon, there were eight Dhūmaketus,

tivaṇṭipupphiyo.meaning_2: name of a monk; (lit.) one who (offered) three-stalked flowers
tivaṇṭipupphiyo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] An epithet used as a proper name. Nominative singular in the text.
tivaṇṭipupphiyo.example_1: itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā tivaṇṭipupphiyo thero imā gāthāyo abhāsitthāti.

tivaṇṭipupphiyattherassāpadānaṃ.meaning_2: the Apadāna of the Elder Tivaṇṭipupphiya; Tivaṇṭipupphiya's Apadāna
tivaṇṭipupphiyattherassāpadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of tivaṇṭipupphiyattherassa + apadānaṃ at the end of a chapter; the title of the tenth Apadāna.

koṭumbarikahatthiyo.meaning_2: Koṭumbarika and Hatthiya (names of two elephants)
koṭumbarikahatthiyo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound of two elephant names; nominative singular in the text.
koṭumbarikahatthiyo.translation_2: Kuṭaja and Bandhujīvī, Koṭumbarika and Hatthiya,

tivaṇṭi.meaning_2: having three sections; consisting of three parts (said of a chapter or group of verses)
tivaṇṭi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Occurs in a verse summary: 'ekacārī tivaṇṭi ca'. Probably a poetic adjective describing a section of three groups; the second element is uncertain (vaṇṭi).
tivaṇṭi.example_2: Ekacārī tivaṇṭi ca, gāthā dvāsaṭṭhi kittitāti.
tivaṇṭi.translation_2: Ekacārī and Tivaṇṭī; sixty-two verses are told.

tamālapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of the Elder Tamālapupphiya; the Apadāna of the Elder Tamālapupphiya
tamālapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title heading of the verse text, nominative singular. Tamālapupphiya is the name of a thera; apadāna means legend or life story. Compound of four parts.

khaṇḍapulliyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: legend of the Elder Khaṇḍapulliya; Khaṇḍapulliya Thera's apadāna
khaṇḍapulliyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of the third chapter of the Apadāna; nominative singular in the text. khaṇḍapulliya is a proper name, sometimes spelled khaṇḍaphulliya.
khaṇḍapulliyattheraapadānaṃ.translation_1: The third legend of Khaṇḍaphulliya Thera.

khaṇḍaphulliyo.meaning_2: name of a monk; the elder Khaṇḍaphulliya
khaṇḍaphulliyo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name of a Thera; nominative singular in the text. Formed from khaṇḍaphulla with the possessive suffix -iya.
khaṇḍaphulliyo.example_1: itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā khaṇḍaphulliyo thero imā gāthāyo abhāsitthāti.

khaṇḍapulliyattherassāpadānaṃ.meaning_2: the Apadāna of Elder Khaṇḍapulliya (the third)
khaṇḍapulliyattherassāpadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Colophon line: it is a sentence-comment, not part of a stanza. Sentence-final, so the nominative ending shows as -ṃ. Khaṇḍapulliyattherassa is itself a compound (khaṇḍapulliya + thera + genitive ending -ssa).
khaṇḍapulliyattherassāpadānaṃ.translation_1: The third legend of Khaṇḍaphulliya Thera is finished.

aṅkolakattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of Aṅkolaka Thera; the Apadāna of Aṅkolaka Thera
aṅkolakattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title heading of the fifth chapter of the Thera-apadāna; nominative singular in the text. Thera name aṅkolaka, a plant name, plus thera and apadāna.
aṅkolakattheraapadānaṃ.translation_1: The fifth legend of Aṅkolaka Thera.

āseko.meaning_2: approaching; sitting down; taking a seat
āseko.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The text has āseko, probably a wrong reading for āsado, a noun made from āsīdati/āsadati with the suffix -a (vuddhi of the root vowel). Nominative singular of an a-stem in -o; the meaning 'approaching; sitting down' comes from the PEU entries for āsada.
āseko.translation_2: “In the thirty-sixth aeon before this, I was Devagajjita,

virohano.meaning_2: growth; growing; causing to grow; producing
virohano.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is nominative singular. The form is also used adjectivally in the sense of 'growing' or 'producing growth'.
virohano.translation_2: There was a water well there, and trees growing tall.

kiṃkaṇikapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of the Elder Kiṅkaṇikapupphiya; the Apadāna of the Elder Kiṅkaṇikapupphiya
kiṃkaṇikapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of the ninth chapter/vagga of the Apadāna; nominative singular in -aṃ, used as a heading. kiṃkaṇika is a flower name (kiṅkaṇipuppha); pupphiya 'having offered flowers'.

chaḷāsītimhito.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of the ablative chaḷāsītimha and ito (from here), used with kappe: 'from the eighty-sixth aeon'. Alternative division: chaḷāsītimhi + ito.
chaḷāsītimhito.translation_2: In the eighty-sixth aeon, one named Apilāpiya,

yūthikaṃ.meaning_2: jasmine flower; flower of the yūthikā creeper (Jasminum auriculatum)
yūthikaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it is the object of paggayha, agreeing with puppha in the compound yūthikaṃ pupphamuttamaṃ; some take yūthika as a shortened yūthikā-puppha. Accusative singular.
yūthikaṃ.translation_2: 54. Lifting up with both hands an unsurpassed jasmine flower,

khaṇḍaphulli.meaning_2: name of a tree (perhaps the Asoka tree); Khaṇḍaphullī
khaṇḍaphulli.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the verse it is listed among trees (with asokiyo); likely a tree name, perhaps the asoka. Could be a feminine form of khaṇḍaphulla. Title-like in the Apadāna.

sereyyo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Proper name in a list of Paccekabuddhas in the Apadāna. Nominative singular in the text. Possibly from seyya (better) but the form is obscure.
sereyyo.translation_2: Bhikkhādāyī, Parivāra, Sereyyo, and likewise Sobhita,

supāricariyopi.meaning_2: Supāricariya (name of a thera; one who serves well)
supāricariyopi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A proper name in the list of theras. In the text it has the emphatic -pi and the sandhi form -opi.
supāricariyopi.translation_2: Chatta and Bandhujīvī, and also Supāricariya,

gāthāni.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text gāthāni is accusative plural, agreeing with chasatāni: 'six hundred verses and sixty-six more'. Some editions read gāthā here; the -āni ending is unusual for a feminine ā-stem and may reflect the vowel of chasatāni (cf. sahassāni).
gāthāni.example_2: Chasatāni ca gāthāni, chasaṭṭhi ca tatuttari.
gāthāni.translation_2: There are six hundred verses and sixty-six more than that.

kaṇikārapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of the Elder Kaṇikārapupphiya; the story of the monk who offered kaṇikāra flowers
kaṇikārapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of the first chapter of the Apadāna, nominative singular in -ṃ. Kaṇikārapupphiya is the name of the thera, derived from kaṇikāra (a flowering tree) + pupphiya (flower-related).
kaṇikārapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.translation_1: The Legend of the Kaṇikāra-flower (Kaṇikārapupphiya) Thera

minelapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the story of the Elder Minelapupphiya
minelapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A verse heading; nominative singular in -aṃ. The first element is probably a proper name, otherwise unknown; the usual title formula would be Minelapupphiyattherassa apadānaṃ.

minelapupphiyattherassāpadānaṃ.meaning_2: the Apadāna of the Elder Minelapupphiya
minelapupphiyattherassāpadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title found at the end of a Apadāna chapter: minela-pupphiya-therassa apadānaṃ, with the final -a elided before a-. Minelapupphiya means 'one who offered the minela flower'. Could be treated as sandhi (masc + nt).

kiṅkaṇipupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of the Elder Kiṅkaṇipupphiya
kiṅkaṇipupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A title heading in the Apadāna. Nominative singular in the text. The name pupphiya is likely from puppha, but the commentarial derivation is uncertain.

dahamoggayha.meaning_2: having plunged into (the lake); having dived into
dahamoggayha.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of dahaṃ + ogayha. ogayha is the absolutive of ogāhati (√gāh with prefix ava), so the whole means 'having plunged into the lake'. The dictionaries read the line as odakaṃ dahaṃ ogayha; consider a separate entry for ogayha itself.
dahamoggayha.translation_2: plunging into a water-tank, the world's chief leader bathed.

sināyi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist-like form in -i (sināyi) used with the sense of bathing; compare nhāyati. The initial s- is a common variant of nh-.
sināyi.translation_2: plunging into a water-tank, the world's chief leader bathed.

taraṇiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of Taraṇiya Thera; the Apadāna of the elder Taraṇiya
taraṇiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title heading of the fourth chapter; nominative singular in -aṃ. Proper name of a thera plus apadāna.

nigguṇḍipupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of the Elder Nigguṇḍipupphiya; the Apadāna of the Elder Nigguṇḍipupphiya
nigguṇḍipupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of an Apadāna chapter (verse 5). pupphiya perhaps 'flower-garlanded' (puppha), but it is a proper name here. Nom. sg. as heading.

salalamāliyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of the elder Salalamāliya; the life story of the venerable Salalamāliya
salalamāliyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A title of a section of the Apadāna, heading verse 7. A compound of four parts; the PEU analysis has salala and apadāna with a variant spelling. Nominative singular in the text.

salalamāliyattherassāpadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of a chapter of the Apadāna. Sandhi of salalamāliyattherassa (genitive singular of salalamāliyatthera, 'Elder Salalamālī') and apadānaṃ ('legacy'). In the text it stands as a section heading, so the case is nominative singular neuter.

koraṇḍapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of the elder Koraṇḍapupphiya; Koraṇḍapupphiya Thera's Apadāna
koraṇḍapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of the eighth chapter of a Theragāthā-apadāna; nominative singular in the text.

koraṇḍapupphiyo.meaning_2: name of a monk; Koraṇḍapupphiya Thera
koraṇḍapupphiyo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Name of a Thera, said to have offered koraṇḍa flowers. Nominative singular in the text; formed with the suffix -iya from koraṇḍapuppha.
koraṇḍapupphiyo.example_1: itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā koraṇḍapupphiyo thero imā gāthāyo abhāsitthāti.
koraṇḍapupphiyo.example_2: Itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā koraṇḍapupphiyo thero imā gāthāyo
koraṇḍapupphiyo.translation_2: Thus indeed the venerable Koraṇḍapupphiya Thera

koraṇḍapupphiyattherassāpadānaṃ.meaning_2: the Apadāna (legend) of the Elder Koraṇḍapupphiya
koraṇḍapupphiyattherassāpadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of the genitive koraṇḍapupphiyattherassa and apadānaṃ; a title at the end of a chapter. The first part is itself a compound: koraṇḍa + pupphiya + thera.

dakado.meaning_2: water-giver; one who gives water; name of a deity (or previous-life name) in the Apadāna
dakado.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound of daka (water) + da (giving, from √dā). Nominative singular in the verse, listed among names (Nigguṇḍipupphī, Salaḷa, Kuraṇḍaka). PEU suggests dakada as an adjective 'giving water' and as a person's name.

salalo.meaning_2: kind of tree; pine tree; (according to commentary) salaḷa tree
salalo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Nominative singular in the text, listed among trees. Associated with kuraṇḍaka; the commentary takes it as a kind of fragrant tree. The identification as a pine is uncertain.

madadiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of mā (negation) + adadi (aorist of dadāti, 'gave'). The text reads madadiṃ with the accusative -ṃ and the following yaṃ nāga belongs to a separate sentence; the sense 'I did not give' is required by the context. The printed form is a sandhi, not a single word.
madadiṃ.example_2: 3. ‘‘ Catunnavutito kappe, yaṃ nāga [dāna (sī. ka.)] madadiṃ tadā;
madadiṃ.translation_2: In the ninety-four aeons since I gave that elephant at that time,

sitaraṃsiṃ.meaning_2: with cool rays; having cool light
sitaraṃsiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sinhalese edition reads sitaraṃsiṃ va; other editions have sataraṃsiṃ, assimilating to the preceding simile of the sun. Accusative singular qualifying bhāṇumaṃ.
sitaraṃsiṃ.example_1: 21. ‘‘ Udentaṃ sataraṃsiṃva, pītaraṃsiṃva [sitaraṃsiṃ va (sī. syā.)] bhāṇumaṃ;
sitaraṃsiṃ.translation_1: “Like the rising hundred-rayed sun, like the sun with cool rays,

anusaṃsāvayiṃ.meaning_2: makes follow with praise; causes to escort; sends off with praise
anusaṃsāvayiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Aorist 1st singular anusaṃsāvayiṃ in the text. Causal form of anusaṃsavati; the PEU suggests 'escort, send off'.

tutideva.meaning_2: name of a king; Tutideva (variant reading)
tutideva.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading (ka.) for Jutideva (syā. dutideva) in the Apadāna verse; taken as a proper name of the aeon's king. The text form is the full sandhi-less compound, not joined to another word.
tutideva.example_1: 49. ‘‘ Ito sattarase kappe, jutideva [dutideva (syā.), tutideva (ka.)] sanāmako;
tutideva.translation_1: “In the seventeenth aeon hence, there was one named Jutideva,

pāpanivārī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it agrees with sappi (ghee), so it is an adjective meaning 'that wards off evil'; the commentary may instead take it as a proper name. Feminine or adjective form of pāpanivāraṇa.
pāpanivārī.translation_2: Sappi and Pāpanivārī, consist of fifty-four verses.

nipuṇavedanī.meaning_2: of subtle understanding; possessing delicate discernment; one who knows subtle matters
nipuṇavedanī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] As the sentence shows (gattañca mudukaṃ mayhaṃ, paññā nipuṇavedanī), it is a feminine nominative describing paññā. PEU analyses it as nipuṇa + vida + yu + ṇi, a possessive compound of nipuṇa and the agent noun vedanī (from √vid, one who knows); resolvable in several ways (e.g. vedī, vidū).
nipuṇavedanī.translation_2: My body is soft and my wisdom has a sharp intellect.

aṅkolapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the story of Aṅkolapupphiya Thera; the Apadāna of the elder Aṅkolapupphiya
aṅkolapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of the sixth chapter of the Aṅkolapupphiyavagga. Nominative singular in the text; functions as a heading rather than a sentence element.

aṅkolapupphiyattherassāpadānaṃ.meaning_2: the Apadāna (legend) of the Elder Aṅkolapupphiya
aṅkolapupphiyattherassāpadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title at the end of a chapter. Sandhi of the Elder's name in the genitive and apadānaṃ; nominative in form but used as a heading. Could also be analysed as a compound (aṅkolapupphiyatthera + apadāna) rather than sandhi.

sovaṇṇavaṭaṃsakiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of the elder Sovaṇṇavaṭaṃsakiya; Sovaṇṇavaṭaṃsakiya Thera's apadāna
sovaṇṇavaṭaṃsakiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title heading of the seventh apadāna in the Apadāna; nominative singular in the text, with the stem-final -a elided before apadānaṃ. Sovaṇṇavaṭaṃsakiya is the name of the elder.

miñjavaṭaṃsakiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of the Elder Miñjavaṭaṃsakiya; title of the eighth chapter of the Apadāna
miñjavaṭaṃsakiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A text title, the eighth vaggas of the Apadāna; nominative singular in the heading. Miñjavaṭaṃsakiya is the name of the thera. Notice the sandhi: thera + apadānaṃ > theraapadānaṃ.

sukatāveḷiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of the Elder Sukatāveḷiya
sukatāveḷiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title heading of a chapter of the Apadāna. Nominative singular in -aṃ; sandhi of -iya + thera gives -iyatthera-.

bakuḷaṃ.meaning_2: Bakula tree (Mimusops elengi); a fragrant flowering tree
bakuḷaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant spelling of bakula, the fragrant bakula tree. Accusative singular in the text, listed among trees and flowers. Sometimes written vakula.
bakuḷaṃ.translation_1: Abyādhi, Aṅkola, Soṇṇa, Miñja, Āveḷa, and Vandana;

sālapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the story of the Elder Sālapupphiya; the legend of the Elder Sālapupphiya
sālapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of a chapter in the Apadāna. Nominative singular ending in -aṃ. Sālapupphiya is the name of the elder, from sāla + pupphiya.
sālapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.translation_1: The Legend of the Elder Sālapupphiya, the third.

piyālapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of Piyālapupphiya Thera; the story of the elder Piyālapupphiya
piyālapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of the seventh chapter of the Apadāna; nominative singular in the text. Piyālapupphiya means 'one who offered piyāla flowers'.

tuvaradāyakattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of Tuvaradāyaka Thera; the Apadāna of the Elder Tuvaradāyaka
tuvaradāyakattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title heading of the first apadāna in the Thera section of the Apadāna; nominative singular in the text. Tuvaradāyaka (tuvarā + dāyaka) refers to the elder who made a gift of a tuvarā (astringent fruit).

tuvaranti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The commentary on this verse (ettha tuvaranti) glosses tuvarati as 'to be like mung or beans', connecting it to tuvara (pigeon pea), not to the root √tur. The form in the text may therefore be a denominative from tuvara, 'is called tuvara', or the word may be a misreading; the Pali reading tuvaraṃ (n. sg. of tuvara) is also possible. Third person plural present.
tuvaranti.example_1: Bharitvā tuvaramādāya [bharitvā turavamādāya (ka.), bhajjitaṃ tuvaramādāya (?) ettha tuvaranti muggakalāyasadisaṃ tuvaraṭṭhinti tadaṭṭhakathā; tuvaro dhaññabhedeti sakkatābhidhāne], saṅghassa adadiṃ ahaṃ.
tuvaranti.translation_1: Having filled a vessel, I took tuvara and gave it to the Saṅgha.

tuvaraṭṭhinti.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Rare word, apparently a kind of grain (muggakalāyasadisaṃ in the commentary). Appears as tuvaraṭṭhinti = tuvaraṭṭhiṃ + iti, accusative singular.
tuvaraṭṭhinti.example_1: Bharitvā tuvaramādāya [bharitvā turavamādāya (ka.), bhajjitaṃ tuvaramādāya (?) ettha tuvaranti muggakalāyasadisaṃ tuvaraṭṭhinti tadaṭṭhakathā; tuvaro dhaññabhedeti sakkatābhidhāne], saṅghassa adadiṃ ahaṃ.
tuvaraṭṭhinti.translation_1: Having filled a vessel, I took tuvara and gave it to the Saṅgha.

tuvaro.meaning_2: pigeon pea (Cajanus cajan); a kind of grain
tuvaro.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Variant reading turava. Commentaries gloss as a grain like muggakalāya. Accusative singular in the text.
tuvaro.example_1: Bharitvā tuvaramādāya [bharitvā turavamādāya (ka.), bhajjitaṃ tuvaramādāya (?) ettha tuvaranti muggakalāyasadisaṃ tuvaraṭṭhinti tadaṭṭhakathā; tuvaro dhaññabhedeti sakkatābhidhāne], saṅghassa adadiṃ ahaṃ.
tuvaro.translation_1: Having filled a vessel, I took tuvara and gave it to the Saṅgha.

tuvarassa.meaning_2: pigeon pea (Cajanus cajan); seed of the pigeon pea
tuvarassa.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Genitive singular in the text (tuvarassa idaṃ phalaṃ = this is the fruit of the pigeon pea). Also neuter and feminine (tuvarī) according to the PEU; the PEU suggests a split tu + vara.
tuvarassa.translation_2: I have come to know no bad destination; this is the fruit of the tuvara.

tuvaradāyakattherassāpadānaṃ.meaning_2: the Apadāna of the Elder Tuvaradāyaka; Tuvaradāyaka Thera's Apadāna
tuvaradāyakattherassāpadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of thera + apadāna (thera + assa? no: therassa + apadāna, with doubling of the initial vowel). Title heading of the first sutta in the Tuvaradāyakatthera-apadāna; nominative singular neuter.

naḷinakesariyo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Name of the elder who spoke these verses. The text has the nominative singular naḷinakesariyo.
naḷinakesariyo.example_1: itthaṃ sudaṃ āyasmā naḷinakesariyo thero imā gāthāyo abhāsitthāti.

naḷinakesariyattherassāpadānaṃ.meaning_2: the Apadāna (legend) of the Elder Naḷinakesari
naḷinakesariyattherassāpadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of the third Apadāna in the Naḷinakesari chapter. Sandhi of ttherassa + apadānaṃ; the whole is a genitive-tatpurisa in form. Doubtful whether the title should be treated as a compound or a sandhi.

viravapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.meaning_2: the legend of Viravapupphiya Thera; the Apadāna of the Elder Viravapupphiya
viravapupphiyattheraapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of the fourth chapter of the Apadāna; nominative singular in the text. The compound probably means 'the Apadāna of the Elder (who offered) virava flowers'.

abhibbhavitvā.meaning_2: having overcome; having vanquished; having surpassed
abhibbhavitvā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] The text's variant abhisaṃbhavitvā in the Suttanipāta supports the same meaning. Absolutive in -tvā.
abhibbhavitvā.translation_1: Having vanquished even all of those problems, one should wander alone, like a rhino’s horn.

kusaṭṭhakadāyakattherassāpadānaṃ.meaning_2: legend of the elder who gave eight food tickets; story of the senior monastic Kusaṭṭhakadāyaka
kusaṭṭhakadāyakattherassāpadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title at the end of a chapter; nominative singular in the text. A compound of kusaṭṭhaka, dāyaka, thera and apadāna (thera + assa as a genitive link).
kusaṭṭhakadāyakattherassāpadānaṃ.translation_1: The sixth legend of Kusaṭṭhakadāyaka Thera is finished.

jhānaparāyanā.meaning_2: devoted to meditation; intent on meditation; whose goal is meditation; finding support in jhāna
jhānaparāyanā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Feminine nominative singular in the text, agreeing with the speaker (nisinnāhaṃ). Describes a meditator whose ultimate support is jhāna.
jhānaparāyanā.translation_1: Everyplace where I am seated, I reach the highest altered states.

vadanañcāpi.meaning_2: and the face too; as well as the face
vadanañcāpi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of vadanaṃ (nominative singular of vadana, 'face') with ca and api. In the text the face is described as disfigured (pabhinnaṃ).
vadanañcāpi.translation_1: And her face was disfigured too, with the putrid stench of a corpse;

tadānugo.meaning_2: following him; his follower; going after him
tadānugo.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] In the text it agrees with the anāgāmī, i.e. 'the non-returner who followed him'. Sometimes analysed as tadā + anuga; the PEU suggests ta + anu + gamu + kvi, so 'one who goes after that (state)' is also possible.
tadānugo.example_1: 139. ‘‘ Arahā āsi so thero, anāgāmī tadānugo;
tadānugo.translation_1: 139. That elder was an arahant, a non-returner followed him.

ticīvaraṃdāsiṃ.meaning_2: I gave a set of three robes
ticīvaraṃdāsiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of ticīvaraṃ (accusative singular) and adāsiṃ (aorist 1st singular of dadāti). The variant reading cīvaraṃ adaṃ supports this analysis.
ticīvaraṃdāsiṃ.example_1: Dhuvaṃ ticīvaraṃdāsiṃ [thūpañca pavaramadaṃ (syā.), dhuvañca cīvaraṃ adaṃ (pī.)], buddhassa lokabandhuno.
ticīvaraṃdāsiṃ.translation_1: I gave robes unceasingly to the Buddha, the Kinsman of the World.

madhurenāhaṃ.meaning_2: by me with a sweet (sound); I with a honey-sweet (sound)
madhurenāhaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of the adjective madhura (instrumental singular) with the pronoun ahaṃ; the -a of madhurena is elided. The adjective agrees with sarena, not with ahaṃ.
madhurenāhaṃ.translation_1: 29. “Having worshipped the Seventh Sage with a sound which was honey-sweet,

adhigayha.meaning_2: having overpowered; having surpassed; having predominated; having mastered
adhigayha.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Absolutive in -ya of adhigaṇhāti (adhi + √gah). In the text it modifies the subject: 'having predominated, I shone'. The PEU gloss 'predominate; surpass' fits.
adhigayha.translation_1: “Having shone through sovereignty, I became the beloved

therāpadānapāḷi.meaning_2: the Therāpadāna Pāḷi; the canonical text of the legends of the elder monks; Book 10 of the Khuddaka Nikāya
therāpadānapāḷi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of a canonical book, appearing in the text as a heading. Themed compound with pāḷi 1 in the sense of 'canonical text'.

buddhaapadānaṃ.meaning_2: legend of the Buddha; Buddha's life story; Book 10 of the Khuddakanikāya (Therāpadāna); lit. Buddha legend
buddhaapadānaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Title of the opening verse of the Apadāna (Therāpadāna). Nominative singular in the text. Sometimes written buddhāpadānaṃ with haplology.

ānandabhaddaṃ.meaning_2: lucky Ānanda; auspicious Ānanda; blessed Ānanda
ānandabhaddaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] A compound of the proper name Ānanda with the adjective bhadda; accusative singular in the verse.
ānandabhaddaṃ.translation_1: Then spoke the Omniscient, Outstanding, Great Sage, to lucky Ānanda with his honeyed voice,

sambodhimukhena.meaning_2: leading to full awakening; with full awakening as the means; headed by enlightenment
sambodhimukhena.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Instrumental singular in the text: "by that means to awakening". The PEU treats it as a bahubbīhi adjective; the final member is mukha 6/7 in the sense of "headed by; means".
sambodhimukhena.translation_1: because that is the means to awaken, wise, they with sharp knowing, through knowledge and power,

sutikkhapaññā.meaning_2: of very sharp understanding; with thoroughly piercing wisdom; exceedingly wise
sutikkhapaññā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Emphatic prefix su + tikkhapaññā, with the second member in composition (paññā + a). Nominative plural in the first sentence, agreeing with the subject; nom sg (or voc) in the second.
sutikkhapaññā.translation_1: because of their wishes and also great strength, do come to attain that state of omniscience.
sutikkhapaññā.example_2: 85. ‘‘‘ Teneva saṃvegamukhena dhīrā, vināpi buddhehi sutikkhapaññā;
sutikkhapaññā.translation_2: 85. “Because that is the means to awaken, wise, they with sharp knowing, through knowledge and power,

sabbaññubhāvaṃ.meaning_2: state of omniscience; omniscient state; state of the all-knowing one
sabbaññubhāvaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the text, object of anupāpuṇanti.
sabbaññubhāvaṃ.translation_1: because of their wishes and also great strength, do come to attain that state of omniscience.

buddhattamabhipatthayiṃ.meaning_2: I aspired to Buddhahood; I longed for the state of a Buddha
buddhattamabhipatthayiṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of buddhattaṃ (accusative) + abhipatthayiṃ (1st person singular aorist). The text reads buddhattam abhipatthayiṃ.
buddhattamabhipatthayiṃ.translation_1: I too among former Buddhas did wish to become a Buddha.

buddhāpadānāni.meaning_2: legends of the Buddhas; life stories of the Buddhas; stories of the Buddha's achievements
buddhāpadānāni.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Plural in the text (nominative/accusative plural -āni) with the verb suṇātha. Could also be analysed as buddhānaṃ apadāna, and the PEU records a variant buddhāpadāniya.
buddhāpadānāni.translation_1: Now listen, with purified minds, to the legends of the Buddhas,

suddhamānasā.meaning_2: with a pure mind; of purified heart; possessing a clean mentality
suddhamānasā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Vocative plural in the text, addressing the listeners. bahubbīhi compound describing the audience.
suddhamānasā.translation_1: Now listen, with purified minds, to the legends of the Buddhas,

tiṃsapāramisampuṇṇā.meaning_2: fulfilled with the thirty perfections; complete in the thirty transcendental virtues
tiṃsapāramisampuṇṇā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] An epithet of the Buddha; the number is left undeclined in the compound (tiṃsa, not tiṃsāya). Nominative plural in the text, agreeing with dhammarājā. The PeU splits it as tiṃsapāramī + sampuṇṇa.
tiṃsapāramisampuṇṇā.translation_1: innumerable Dhamma-kings who fulfilled thirty perfections.

dasaṅgulī.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Used of the Buddha's hands. Nominative singular in the text.
dasaṅgulī.translation_1: those World-Chiefs with followers and the Best Buddhas’ Awakening.

vijjantisaṅkhiyā.meaning_2: existing and to be reckoned; that exist and can be counted; as many as exist
vijjantisaṅkhiyā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of vijjanti (present 3rd plural of vijjati 1, 'exist') and saṅkhiyā (nominative plural of the potential participle saṅkhiya, 'to be reckoned'). The phrase ratanā vijjantisaṅkhiyā means 'as many jewels as exist'. Written vijjanti saṅkhiyā in some editions.
vijjantisaṅkhiyā.translation_1: I brought it all forth with my mind: things on the ground and in the sky,

sabbamāhariṃ.meaning_2: I carried off everything; I brought all
sabbamāhariṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Sandhi of sabbaṃ (accusative of sabba) and āhariṃ (1st singular aorist of āharati, 'carried here; brought'). The sandhi is -aṃ + ā- > -amā-. In the verse, the speaker gathered all gems, whether in the sky or on the earth, by mind.
sabbamāhariṃ.example_1: Ākāsaṭṭhā ca bhūmaṭṭhā [bhummaṭṭhā (sī. syā.)], manasā sabbamāhariṃ.
sabbamāhariṃ.translation_1: uncountable as are the gems found in the fields of the Buddhas.

rūpiyabhūmiyaṃ.meaning_2: made of silver; with a silver-finished ground; having silver flooring
rūpiyabhūmiyaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Locative singular in the text, describing the palace (pāsādaṃ). The PEU splits it as rūpiyabhūmi + ka, but since the meaning is 'made of silver' the -ya suffix (cf. PEU's kiu) fits better; cf. rūpiya 1 'silver; money'. Could also be read as a tatpuruṣa adjective 'whose ground is silver'.
rūpiyabhūmiyaṃ.translation_1: I created a palace there, with a floor made out of silver.

nekabhummaṃ.meaning_2: having many floors; with many stories
nekabhummaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Attributive adjective modifying a mansion or palace; accusative singular neuter agreeing with the noun in the sentence. Could also be analysed as a bahubbīhi compound ("having many floors").
nekabhummaṃ.translation_1: Various floors made out of gems arose and stretched up toward the sky.

nabhamuggataṃ.meaning_2: risen up into the sky; reaching up to the sky; soaring into the heavens
nabhamuggataṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Compound of nabhaṃ (accusative of nabhas, "sky") + uggata (pp of uggacchati, "gone up"). Nominative singular neuter agreeing with vimānaṃ in the second verse; the form in the text could also be read as nominative singular neuter of the compound. The first verse's ubbiddhaṃ agrees similarly.
nabhamuggataṃ.translation_1: Various floors made out of gems arose and stretched up toward the sky.
nabhamuggataṃ.translation_2: and a mansion one hundred and fifty hands wide, raised up into the sky.

vicittathambhaṃ.meaning_2: with diverse pillars; with variegated columns; having multi-coloured posts; lit. variegated pillar
vicittathambhaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Bahubbīhi compound describing a building. Nominative singular in the verse, agreeing with the implied structure (sukataṃ, suvibhattaṃ).
vicittathambhaṃ.translation_1: There were varied well-made pillars, well-proportioned, very costly.

kanakamayasaṅghāṭaṃ.meaning_2: golden assemblage; mass made of gold; golden beam
kanakamayasaṅghāṭaṃ.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Accusative singular in the verse. PEU glosses 'assemblage (such as a beam) made of gold'; the exact architectural referent is uncertain.
kanakamayasaṅghāṭaṃ.translation_1: The central beam was made of gold, the gate was canopy-adorned.

kontacchattehi.meaning_2: parasol topped with a sceptre; sunshade with a lance finial
kontacchattehi.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Instrumental plural in the text (kontacchattehi). Describes decorated sunshades with lance-like finials; the reading may be connected with kanakacchatta.
kontacchattehi.translation_1: The central beam was made of gold, the gate was canopy-adorned.

vimalabbhasamā.meaning_2: like a stainless cloud; pure as a cloud; lit. stainless cloud like
vimalabbhasamā.comment: [deepseek: deepseek-v4-flash] Three-part compound; the second member abbha is not given in the related entries. Feminine singular agreeing with bhūmi in the verse.
vimalabbhasamā.translation_1: The first floor, lapis lazuli, was lovely as a stainless cloud.
